definition_zh: 视力；视觉；所见景象；愿景；远见；幻象；影像；极美的人或物
definition_en: the power of seeing, and also whatever is seen or imagined, especially a picture of a future worth working toward
core_image: 暗房里一束光穿过透镜落在白纸上，纸上浮出远处山脊的轮廓
scene: 镜头调好后，远处山脊的轮廓第一次清晰地落进取景框。The telescope's lens brought the distant ridge into vision for the first time.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「看见远处事物的能力」（第 1 个义项：眼睛借光线辨认远处物体的能力）；句意为望远镜的镜片第一次把远处山脊带入视野。图中可辨识物件：透镜、山脊、取景框、清晨的天光。

pos.zh: 所见景象；幻象；影像（可数）
愿景；远见（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 有远见的；空想的 / 空想家

senses.title: The power of seeing
senses.definition: the ability of the eyes to receive light and make out shapes, distance and colour
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛接收光线、辨认形状、远近与颜色的能力
senses.example: Regular eye tests catch slow changes in vision before they become serious.
senses.exampleCN: 定期检查眼睛能在视力变化变严重之前发现它。
senses.why: The word first named the act of seeing itself, so the faculty that makes seeing possible is the same event viewed as a capacity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就指「看见」这个动作，因此使看见得以发生的能力，是同一件事被当作一种本领来看。

senses.title: Something that appears before the eyes
senses.definition: a sight that presents itself to a viewer, especially one that is striking
senses.definitionCN: 呈现在观看者眼前的一景，尤指引人注目者
senses.example: From the ridge they had a vision of the whole valley lying under mist.
senses.exampleCN: 站在山脊上，他们看见整个山谷躺在雾下。
senses.why: What the eyes receive was not separated from the act of receiving in the older use, so the object seen kept the same name.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里，眼睛接收到的东西与接收这个动作并未分开，因此所见之物沿用了同一个名称。

senses.title: A picture of a desired future
senses.titleCN: 愿景；对理想未来的构想
senses.definition: a picture of what an organization or a person wants to bring about, used to guide long-term plans
senses.definitionCN: 组织或个人希望实现的未来图景，用来指导长期计划
senses.example: The founders set out a vision of a city where nobody needs a car.
senses.exampleCN: 创办者提出了一个人人都不需要汽车的城市愿景。
senses.why: A future state must be imagined before it is built, so the word moved from outer sight to inner sight and then to a shared plan.
senses.whyCN: 未来的状态必须先被想象出来才能建造，于是这个词从外在的看见转向内在的看见，再成为共享的计划。

senses.title: Foresight in practical matters
senses.definition: the ability to see what is likely to happen and to act on it early
senses.definitionCN: 看出事情可能如何发展并及早行动的能力
senses.example: Her vision caught the shift in the market years before her rivals did.
senses.exampleCN: 她在竞争对手之前好几年就看清了市场的转向。
senses.why: Foresight is literally seeing ahead, so a person who plans for what has not happened is using the same image.
senses.whyCN: 远见字面上就是「看见前方」，因此为尚未发生的事作准备的人，用的仍是同一幅图。

senses.title: An apparition seen without a body
senses.definition: something that appears to a person in a religious or hallucinated experience without physical presence
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教体验或幻觉中出现、并无实体的事物
senses.example: The hermit said a vision of light had stood above the altar.
senses.exampleCN: 这位隐修者说有一团光的异象立在祭坛上方。
senses.why: An apparition keeps the frame of seeing but drops the object that can be touched, which is why the word was borrowed for such experiences.
senses.whyCN: 异象保留了「看见」的框架，却去掉了可触摸的实体，因此这类体验借用了这个词。

senses.title: An image formed by a lens or screen
senses.titleCN: 镜片或屏幕上成的影像
senses.definition: the image that an optical instrument or a display produces
senses.definitionCN: 光学仪器或显示屏所产生的图像
senses.example: A slit lamp gives the doctor a magnified vision of the front of the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 裂隙灯让医生看到眼前部被放大的影像。
senses.why: Optics kept the literal sense: a lens forms an image, and that image is still what is seen.
senses.whyCN: 光学保留了字面义：镜片生成一个像，而这个像仍然是「被看见的东西」。

senses.title: A particular way of seeing a subject
senses.titleCN: 视角；对某一问题的看法
senses.definition: a distinct way of understanding or presenting a subject
senses.definitionCN: 理解或呈现某一问题的独特方式
senses.example: The book offers a vision of history written from below.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书提供了一种自下而上写历史的视角。
senses.why: A way of reading facts is a picture held in the mind, so a perspective is called a vision of the subject.
senses.whyCN: 解读事实的方式是心里持有一幅图，因此一种视角也被称为对那个问题的一种「看见」。

senses.title: A person or thing of striking beauty
senses.titleCN: 极美的人或物（文学用法）
senses.definition: a person or object whose beauty is so unusual that seeing it feels like a revelation
senses.definitionCN: 美得非同寻常、见之如受启示的人或物
senses.example: In the white gown she was a vision at the top of the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着白色长裙站在楼梯顶端，美得像幻影。
senses.why: The literary sense uses the same shock of seeing: something so beautiful that it seems more revealed than present.
senses.whyCN: 这一文学义用的是同一种看见的震动：美到仿佛不是在场，而是被显现出来。

intro.en: Vision entered English through Old French from Latin visio 'a seeing', built on the verb videre 'to see'. The pre-Latin root behind videre is reconstructed rather than attested. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语表示「看见」的名词，其基础动词亦为「看见」。该动词之前的词根属重构形式，并无实物书证。年代均为约数。

items.en: Videre meant 'to see' and in some phrases 'to know', since seeing was treated as a form of knowing. Its older root is reconstructed; no attested pre-Latin form survives, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，在某些说法里也表示「知道」，因为看见被当作一种认识。它更早的词根属重构形式，拉丁语之前没有实际书证，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Visio, built on the past participle visus plus the noun suffix -io, named the act of seeing and then the thing seen.
items.cn: visio 由过去分词 visus 加名词后缀 -io 构成，先指看见这一动作，再指所见之物。

items.en: Old French vision carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, where it was used first for eyesight and for religious apparitions.
items.cn: 古法语的这个名词在十三世纪进入英语，最初用于视力，也用于宗教异象。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word was applied to imaginative foresight, a picture of what a person intends to bring about.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词被用于想象性的预见，即一个人打算促成的图景。

items.en: In the twentieth century a short written statement of long-term aims took the name vision statement, which fixed the planning sense in ordinary use.
items.cn: 二十世纪，一段简短陈述长期目标的文字被称为愿景宣言，这把「规划」义固定到日常用法中。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like vision but come from other roots or other prefixes; group two holds words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形似而来源不同、或前缀不同的词；第二组是语义上与本词重叠的词。

entries.definition: From dividere 'to divide', not from videre: it is a splitting, so the shared ending hides two unrelated verbs.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 dividere「分开」，而非 videre：它是分割，相同的词尾掩盖了两个无关的动词。

entries.definition: Pro- 'ahead' plus videre 'see': seeing ahead became supplying what will be needed, hence a stock or a clause in a law.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「在前」加 videre「看见」：预先看见后来变成预备所需之物，因此指储备或法律条款。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus videre: to look at something a second time in order to change it.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再次」加 videre：为修改而再看一遍。

entries.definition: Greek tele 'far' joined to the Latin noun for a sight: a device that brings distant images home.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 tele「远」加上拉丁的「所见」名词：把远处影像带到眼前的装置。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for both the faculty and what is seen; vision is its more formal and more future-oriented relative.
entries.definitionCN: 兼指视力与所见之物的日常词；本词更正式，也更常指向未来。

entries.definition: Strictly the physical power of the eyes, with nothing about imagination or plans.
entries.definitionCN: 严格指眼睛的生理能力，不涉及想象或计划。

entries.definition: The practical ability to anticipate; it lacks the inspiring, shared picture that a vision carries.
entries.definitionCN: 务实的预判能力；缺少本词那种鼓舞人心的共享图景。

entries.definition: The general power to form images in the mind, with no claim that they will come true.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指在心里形成形象的能力，并不主张这些形象会成真。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb for seeing followed by a noun suffix: first the act of seeing, then the thing seen.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「看见」动词加名词后缀：先指看见这一动作，再指所见之物。

normal.en: The same root splits into three lines: the adjective for sight, the verb for forming a picture, and the noun for a person who sees ahead.
normal.cn: 同一词根分出三条线：表示视觉的形容词、表示在心里成像的动词，以及表示有远见者的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the layers: blurred vision, night vision, field of vision, vision statement.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出层次：视力模糊、夜视、视野、愿景宣言。

normal.en: Optics never lost the literal sense: a lens still forms an image that is called what the eye receives.
normal.cn: 光学从未丢掉字面义：镜片成的像仍用眼睛所接收之物的名称。

normal.en: A company's written vision statement shows how a plan became a document.
normal.cn: 公司的愿景宣言说明书面的计划如何变成一纸文件。

abstract.en: Picture a person at the door of a dark room who first sees a line of light and then a whole mountain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在暗房门口，先看见一线光，再看见整座山。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tracing the outline of a district that has not been built yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手先描出一片尚未建成的城区的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a white figure at the end of a stage, so bright that the audience forgets to breathe.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台尽头一个白色身影，亮得让观众忘了呼吸。

examples.en: The survey asked workers what vision they held for the company in ten years.
examples.cn: 调查问员工，他们对公司十年后的样子抱有什么愿景。

examples.en: Smoke reduced the driver's vision to a few metres.
examples.cn: 烟雾把司机的可视距离缩短到几米。

examples.en: The novel ends with a vision of the sea rising over the town.
examples.cn: 小说以海水漫过小镇的幻景收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vis（看）+ ion（名词）」——看见的东西 → 视力、景象，进而「看见未来」→ 愿景、远见

root: 拉丁语「看见」动词加名词后缀构成「看见、所见」这一名词；该动词更早的印欧词根属重构形式，无实际书证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: light enters an eye, a shape is seen, the shape is named, then what does not yet exist is seen, then the inner eye, the lens, the angle of viewing and finally beauty that stops the viewer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：光进入眼睛，形状被看见并被命名，接着尚未存在的东西被看见，然后是内在之眼、镜片、观看的角度，最后是让人停住呼吸的美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light in a dark room passing through a lens and printing the outline of a distant ridge on paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗房里一束光穿过透镜，把远处山脊的轮廓印在纸上。

branches.en: OPTICAL SEEING: eyesight and a lens image are the same light falling on a surface.
branches.cn: 光学的看见：视力与镜片成像，都是同一束光落在一个面上。

branches.en: STRIKING SIGHT: a rare view and a beautiful figure both stop the person who sees them.
branches.cn: 夺目之景：罕见的景色与极美的人影，都让看见的人停住。

branches.en: SEEING AHEAD: a shared picture of the future and private foresight differ only in who holds the picture.
branches.cn: 看见前方：共享的未来图景与个人的远见，只差在谁持有这幅图。

branches.en: APPARITION: what is seen without a body keeps the frame of seeing and loses the object.
branches.cn: 异象：没有实体的所见，保留了看见的框架，失去了对象。

branches.en: PERSPECTIVE: a way of reading facts is a picture held in the mind.
branches.cn: 视角：解读事实的方式，是心里持有一幅图。

intro.en: Vision is a Latin noun built from a verb of seeing plus a noun suffix, and the same root also yields adjectives, verbs and compounds.
intro.cn: 这是一个由拉丁语「看见」动词加名词后缀构成的名词，同一词根还给出形容词、动词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives vision, visual and visible; visus supplies the noun of sight; tele- from Greek adds the idea of distance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「看见」动词衍生出表示视觉与可见的形容词；其过去分词提供「所见」的名词；希腊语表示「远」的成分加上距离的意思。

items.structure: videre, vidi, visum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: The root carries the act of seeing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「看见」这一动作。

items.example: The noun named both the act and its object.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指动作与对象。

items.meaning: act or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成名词。

items.example: Vision still means seeing before it means a plan.
items.exampleCN: 这个词先指看见，然后才指计划。

items.example: A visual record is one made to be seen.
items.exampleCN: 视觉记录就是为被看见而做的记录。

items.meaning: to form a picture in the mind
items.example: Athletes visualize the jump before they attempt it.
items.exampleCN: 运动员在起跳前先在脑中过一遍动作。

items.meaning: the act of making something pictorial
items.example: The mapping software produces a clear visualization of the data.
items.exampleCN: 制图软件把数据做成清晰的图像。

items.meaning: given to seeing ahead; a person so gifted
items.example: The plan was the work of a single visionary.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划出自一位有远见者之手。

items.meaning: a device showing images from far away
items.example: Television joined a Greek distance word to the Latin noun for a sight.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把希腊的距离词接到拉丁的「所见」名词上。

definition_zh: 程序；步骤；手续；医疗操作；议事规程；子程序；工序
definition_en: a fixed set of steps that must be followed to carry out a task, a formal process or a medical treatment
core_image: 手术室外的走廊上，一张写满步骤的卡片贴在墙上，医生拿笔逐项打勾
scene: 手术开始前，主刀医生和护士对着墙上的步骤卡逐项核对了一遍。The team followed the written procedure step by step before the operation began.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「为完成某事而必须依次执行的一套步骤」（第 1 个义项：固定顺序的操作步骤）；句意为手术开始前，团队按书面步骤逐项执行。图中可辨识物件：步骤卡、打勾用的笔、手术室门、走廊指示灯。

derivatives.zh: 进行中的事项；诉讼程序

senses.title: A fixed series of steps
senses.definition: an ordered set of actions that must be followed to complete a task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项任务而必须依次执行的一组动作
senses.example: The lab has a written procedure for handling every sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室对每一个样本的处理都有书面步骤。
senses.why: The word came from a verb meaning to go forward, so a procedure is a path laid out to be walked in order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自意为「向前走」的动词，因此程序就是一条铺好、须按顺序走完的路线。

senses.title: The official way of handling a matter
senses.definition: the recognized sequence by which an official body accepts, hears or decides something
senses.definitionCN: 官方机构受理、审议或决定某事所认可的次序
senses.example: The complaint went through the standard procedure for appeals.
senses.exampleCN: 这项投诉走了标准的上诉手续。
senses.why: Anything a body must do in a set order becomes a procedure, because the order is what makes the decision valid.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须按固定次序完成的事都叫程序，因为正是这个次序使决定有效。

senses.title: A medical treatment that acts on the body
senses.definition: a treatment in which a doctor performs a defined action on or inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 医生在体表或体内施行的一套明确操作
senses.example: The procedure took forty minutes and needed no overnight stay.
senses.exampleCN: 这台操作用了四十分钟，不需要留院过夜。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for any defined course of action on a patient, and the sense narrowed to interventions.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词指对病人的一套明确处置，后来收窄为各种介入操作。

senses.title: The accepted order of business in a meeting
senses.definition: the rules that govern how a meeting or assembly conducts its business
senses.definitionCN: 会议或议会处理事务时遵循的规则
senses.example: The chair reminded the committee of its own procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 主席提醒委员会注意自己定的议事规程。
senses.why: A meeting is valid only if it moves through the agreed steps, so the rules of order took this name.
senses.whyCN: 会议只有按商定的步骤推进才有效，因此议事规则也用了这个名称。

senses.title: A named block of code in a program
senses.definition: a section of a program that performs one task and returns control to the point that called it
senses.definitionCN: 程序中完成单项任务并把控制权交回调用处的一段代码
senses.example: The program calls the same procedure every time it reads a record.
senses.exampleCN: 程序每读一条记录就调用同一个子程序。
senses.why: Computing reused the word for a routine because a routine is a small ordered path through the machine's work.
senses.whyCN: 计算机把这个词用于例行程序，因为一段例程就是机器工作中一条小型有序路径。

senses.title: The usual way a job is done in a place
senses.definition: the established way of doing a job in a particular workplace, whether or not it is written down
senses.definitionCN: 某一工作场所既定的做事方式，无论是否写成文字
senses.example: Checking the seals twice is procedure on this rig, not a personal habit.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座钻井平台上，密封件查两遍是规程，不是个人习惯。
senses.why: An unwritten habit becomes procedure once a crew treats it as the required order, so the word covers custom as well as rule.
senses.whyCN: 一旦班组把它当作必须遵循的次序，未成文的习惯也成了程序，因此这个词兼指惯例与规章。

senses.title: The steps by which a case moves through court
senses.definition: the rules that fix what a party must file, when and in what form during litigation
senses.definitionCN: 规定当事人在诉讼中须提交什么、何时提交、以何种形式提交的规则
senses.example: Civil procedure decides what a plaintiff must file and when.
senses.exampleCN: 民事诉讼程序决定原告必须提交什么、何时提交。
senses.why: Legal systems separate substance from steps, and the steps are called procedure because they carry a case forward in order.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系把实体与步骤分开，而这些步骤被称为程序，因为它们按次序把一个案子往前推进。

senses.title: One stage in an industrial process
senses.titleCN: 工序；工艺流程中的一环
senses.definition: a single defined operation within a manufacturing or chemical sequence
senses.definitionCN: 制造或化工流程中一道界限明确的加工步骤
senses.example: Each procedure in the line has its own temperature range.
senses.exampleCN: 流水线上每一道工序都有自己的温度区间。
senses.why: A factory breaks a long making into ordered steps, and each step inherits the name of the whole path.
senses.whyCN: 工厂把漫长的制造拆成有序步骤，每一道步骤都继承了整条路径的名称。

intro.en: Procedure came through French from Latin procedere 'to go forward', built on pro- 'forward' and cedere 'to go, to yield'. The pre-Latin root of cedere is a reconstruction. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语「向前走」的动词，由意为「向前」的前缀与意为「走、让」的动词构成。后者更早的词根属重构形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, to withdraw, to yield'. Its deeper origin is not attested; the root usually proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、退、让」。其更深来源没有书证；通常为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus cedere produced procedere 'to go forward, to advance, to continue'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 cedere 构成 procedere，意为「向前走、推进、继续」。

items.en: Late and Medieval Latin formed procedura for the manner of proceeding in a matter, especially in law.
items.cn: 晚期与中世纪拉丁语构成 procedura，指处理某事的进行方式，尤用于法律。

items.en: French procédure brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as the conduct of a legal action.
items.cn: 法语 procédure 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指法律诉讼的进行方式。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word covered meeting rules, from the nineteenth medical interventions, and from the twentieth a block of code in computing.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个词涵盖议事规则；十九世纪起涵盖医疗介入；二十世纪起涵盖计算机中的代码段。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin verb of going, plus one word of Greek origin that looks similar; group two holds words for ways of doing things.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「走」动词的词，外加一个形似而来源不同的希腊词；第二组是表示做事方式的近义词。

entries.definition: A continuous course of change rather than an ordered checklist; the same Latin verb, a different noun suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 指连续变化的过程，而非有序清单；同一拉丁动词，名词后缀不同。

entries.definition: The carrying on of an action, or its record in court; it names the activity, not the rules for it.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的进行，或其在法庭上的记录；它指活动本身，而不是活动的规则。

entries.definition: Pra- 'before' plus cedere: something that went before and now guides later decisions, not a set of steps.
entries.definitionCN: pra-「在前」加 cedere：先前发生、如今指导后续决定的事例，不是一套步骤。

entries.definition: From Greek protokollon, the first sheet glued to a roll; it became a diplomatic or technical code, not a Latin path.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊语「贴在卷首的第一张纸」，后来指外交或技术约定，与拉丁的「路径」无关。

entries.definition: A systematic way of doing something, often chosen by the doer rather than imposed by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性的做法，常由执行者自行选择，而非由权威规定。

entries.definition: A regular way of doing something because it is familiar and repeated, with no claim of formal validity.
entries.definitionCN: 因熟悉而重复的惯常做法，并不强调正式效力。

entries.definition: A single action in a sequence; a procedure is the whole sequence of such actions.
entries.definitionCN: 序列中的单个动作；程序则是这些动作的整个序列。

entries.definition: The organized set of parts and rules taken together, wider than one procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 由各部分与规则构成的整体安排，比单个程序更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: 'Forward' plus 'to go': a procedure is a path laid out so that work can be walked through in order.
normal.cn: 「向前」加「走」：程序就是一条铺好的路径，让工作按顺序走完。

normal.en: The same verb yields the verb to continue, the noun for a court record and the word for a continuous process.
normal.cn: 同一动词还给出表示「继续」的动词、表示法庭记录的名词，以及表示连续过程的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: standard procedure, safety procedure, legal procedure, surgical procedure.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：标准程序、安全规程、法律程序、外科手术。

normal.en: A hospital, a court and a committee each keep a written path that must be followed in order.
normal.cn: 医院、法院与委员会各自都有一份必须按顺序走完的书面路径。

normal.en: Computing calls a small ordered routine a procedure because it is a short path through the machine's work.
normal.cn: 计算机把一小段有序例程称为子程序，因为它是机器工作中一条短路径。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor with numbered doors, each of which must be opened before the next one.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每隔一段有一扇编号的门，必须依次打开。

abstract.en: Picture a dance notation that only works if every count is danced in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一份舞谱，只有每一拍都踩准才成立。

abstract.en: Picture a legal file that is valid only because every stamp sits in the right order.
abstract.cn: 想象一份法律卷宗，只因每枚印章次序正确才有效。

examples.en: Changing the procedure required the approval of the whole committee.
examples.cn: 更改程序需要全体委员会批准。

examples.en: The surgeon explained the procedure to the family in plain words.
examples.cn: 外科医生用平实的话向家属解释了这台手术。

examples.en: A missing signature sent the file back to the start of the procedure.
examples.cn: 少了一个签名，文件被退回程序的起点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ ced（走）+ ure（名词）」——一路向前走完的路线 → 程序、步骤、手续

root: 拉丁语「向前走」的动词由意为「向前」的前缀与意为「走、让」的动词构成，加名词后缀再构成「进行方式」；该动词更早的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one path: a set of steps is laid down, then adopted by an office, applied to a body, imposed on a meeting, coded into a machine, hardened into local custom, stretched into litigation and finally shortened to one stage on a factory line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条路径展开：先铺下一套步骤，再被机构采用、施于身体、用于会议、写进机器，固化为本地惯例，延伸为诉讼，最后缩短为工厂流水线上的一环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered card on the wall of a hospital corridor, each line ticked in order before anyone may proceed.
core.cn: 核心意象：医院走廊墙上一张编号卡片，每一行都按顺序打勾后才允许继续。

branches.en: LAID PATH AND LOCAL HABIT: a written sequence and an unwritten one are the same order once a crew treats it as required.
branches.cn: 铺好的路径与本地习惯：书面次序与未成文次序，一旦被班组视为必须，便是同一种次序。

branches.en: FORMAL VALIDITY: what an office accepts and what a court requires are both orders that make a result valid.
branches.cn: 正式效力：机构受理与法院要求，都是使结果有效的次序。

branches.en: ONE OPERATION: a treatment on a body and a stage on a line are single steps cut out of a longer path.
branches.cn: 单次操作：施于身体的一台操作与流水线上的一道工序，都是从更长路径中截出的单步。

branches.en: RULES OF ORDER: a meeting valid only if it moves through the agreed steps.
branches.cn: 议事规则：会议只有按商定步骤推进才有效。

branches.en: CODED PATH: computing writes the same ordered path into a block of instructions.
branches.cn: 编码路径：计算机把同一条有序路径写成一段指令。

intro.en: Procedure is a Latin noun of path and motion: a prefix meaning forward, a verb meaning to go, and a noun suffix marking the result.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示路径与运动的拉丁名词：一个意为「向前」的前缀、一个意为「走」的动词，以及标记结果的名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere gives proceed, process, precede and succeed; pro- adds forward motion; the noun suffix marks a way of doing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「走」动词衍生出继续、过程、先于与接着等词；「向前」前缀加进向前的运动；名词后缀标记一种做法。

items.structure: cedere, cessi, cessum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root carries movement along a line.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载沿一条线移动的意思。

items.example: The prefix fixes the direction of the movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀确定运动的方向。

items.example: The verb is the whole path in one word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用一个词表达了整条路径。

items.example: The noun turned the path into a thing that can be written down.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把路径变成可以写下来的东西。

items.example: The English noun still means a path to be walked.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词仍指一条要走完的路径。

items.meaning: result or instrument of an action
items.example: The suffix marks the outcome of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记动词的结果。

items.meaning: relating to steps or formal rules
items.meaningCN: 与步骤或正式规则有关的
items.example: A procedural objection concerns how a decision was made.
items.exampleCN: 程序性异议针对决定是怎么样作出的。

items.example: The train proceeded once the signal changed.
items.exampleCN: 信号一变，列车继续前行。

items.example: The same verb, seen as a flowing course rather than a checklist.
items.exampleCN: 同一个动词，被看作流动的过程而非清单。

latinEntries.meaning: to go, to withdraw, to yield

definition_zh: 运转；操作；手术；行动；业务；运算；经营单位
definition_en: the working of a machine or system, a planned activity, a surgical treatment, or a mathematical process
core_image: 手术灯下，主刀医生的手停在心脏上方，旁边屏幕上跳动着体外循环机的运行曲线
scene: 手术灯亮起后，主刀医生用两个小时完成了孩子心脏上的一处修补。The hospital performed a delicate operation on the child's heart that morning.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「在身体上施行的外科手术」（第 3 个义项：由医生切开或进入体内完成的治疗）；句意为那天上午医院为孩子的心脏做了一台精细手术。图中可辨识物件：手术灯、体外循环机、监护屏、无菌手套。

pos.zh: 行动；业务；经营单位（可数）

senses.title: The working of a machine or system
senses.definition: the way in which a device, plant or system performs its function
senses.definitionCN: 装置、工厂或系统发挥功能的方式
senses.example: The pump's operation is monitored from a control room.
senses.exampleCN: 泵的运转由控制室监控。
senses.why: The word rests on a Latin verb meaning to work, so the working of a system is its most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「工作」动词之上，因此系统的运转是它最字面的义项。

senses.title: The act of making a device work
senses.definition: the act of running or controlling a machine by hand or by control
senses.definitionCN: 用手或控制装置使机器运行的动作
senses.example: Operation of the crane requires two trained hands.
senses.exampleCN: 操作这台吊车需要两名受过训练的人。
senses.why: Doing the work and making something else work are two sides of one verb, so the act of driving a machine took the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自己干活与让别的东西干活是同一个动词的两面，因此驱动机器的动作也用了这个名词。

senses.title: A surgical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment in which a surgeon cuts into or enters the body to repair it
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生切开或进入体内进行修补的治疗
senses.example: The operation on her knee lasted two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖的手术持续了两个小时。
senses.why: Surgery is work done on a body, so medicine used the general noun for work and it became the everyday word for an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 手术是对身体所做的工作，因此医学用这个泛指「工作」的名词，它后来成了介入治疗的日常说法。

senses.title: A planned military action
senses.definition: an organized movement of forces with a set aim, usually given a name
senses.definitionCN: 有明确目标、通常有代号的部队组织行动
senses.example: The rescue operation began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在黎明开始。
senses.why: Military staffs speak of work done by combined forces as one operation, and the sense spread to any coordinated action.
senses.whyCN: 军事参谋把多支部队合力完成的工作称为一次行动，这个义项后来扩展到任何协同行动。

senses.title: The everyday activities of a business
senses.definition: the routine activities by which a company or institution keeps running, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构维持运转的日常活动，常用复数
senses.example: The firm moved its operations closer to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把业务迁到离港口更近的地方。
senses.why: A business is a set of workings, so its routine activities are called its operations rather than its plans.
senses.whyCN: 一家企业就是一组运转，因此它的日常活动被称为业务，而不是计划。

senses.title: A mathematical process
senses.definition: a rule applied to numbers or symbols to produce a new value
senses.definitionCN: 施于数字或符号以得出新值的规则
senses.example: Addition is the first operation children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 加法是孩子学的第一种运算。
senses.why: Mathematics treats each rule as work performed on symbols, which is the same idea of a working applied to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 数学把每条规则看作对符号所做的工作，这与「运转」是同一个意思，只是对象换成数字。

senses.title: A running business or unit
senses.definition: an enterprise or a distinct unit that is being run as a going concern
senses.definitionCN: 作为持续经营体运作的企业或独立单位
senses.example: The mine is a profitable operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿是一个盈利的经营单位。
senses.why: Once a business is seen as something that works, the thing that works can itself be called an operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦企业被看作在运转的东西，这个在运转的东西本身就可以被称为一个经营单位。

senses.title: An organized piece of work with a plan
senses.titleCN: 有组织的行动；专项行动
senses.definition: a coordinated piece of work, often large, carried out by a group toward one aim
senses.definitionCN: 由一群人朝同一目标实施的、常具规模的协同工作
senses.example: The cleanup operation involved three hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次清理行动动用了三百名志愿者。
senses.why: Any large piece of coordinated work can be called an operation, because it is work organized as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 任何大规模协同工作都可称为一次行动，因为它被组织成一个整体的运作。

intro.en: Operation came through Old French from Latin operatio 'a working', built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. The origin of opus before Latin is unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语表示「工作」的名词，其基础为表示「工作」的动词与名词。名词词根在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work, a task'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品、任务」。其在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，有时为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Operari, a deponent verb, meant 'to work, to labour, to perform'.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为「工作、劳作、施行」。

items.en: Operatio, from operari plus the noun suffix -io, named a working or the result of working.
items.cn: operatio 由 operari 加名词后缀 -io 构成，指工作这一动作或其结果。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first for any action or effect.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指任何动作或效果。

items.en: From the seventeenth century surgery adopted the word for an intervention, and from the eighteenth military staffs used it for a named action.
items.cn: 十七世纪起外科把这个词用于介入治疗，十八世纪起军事参谋用它指有代号的行动。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin noun of work, plus one that only looks similar; group two holds words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「工作」名词的词，外加一个仅形似的词；第二组是语义上与本词重叠的词。

entries.definition: To run a machine, to carry on business or to perform surgery; the noun names the working, the verb performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指运转机器、开展业务或施行手术；名词指运转本身，动词指施行。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine or a business, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指操作机器或经营业务的人。

entries.definition: Co- 'together' plus the same verb: joint work, with no single unit of action.
entries.definitionCN: co-「共同」加同一动词：指共同工作，不指单个动作单元。

entries.definition: From orare 'to speak', not from opus: a formal speech, similar only in its ending.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 orare「说话」，而非 opus：指正式演说，仅词尾相似。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine and the procedure itself, with nothing about machines or business.
entries.definitionCN: 指外科这一学科及手术本身，与机器或业务无关。

entries.definition: The ordered steps of an action; it does not imply that anything is actually running.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的有序步骤，并不表示事情真的在运转。

entries.definition: The proper role or capacity of a part; it names what something is for, not how it runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指某部件的应有作用或能力，说明它用于什么，而非如何运转。

entries.definition: A connected series of actions for one aim, often public or military; it stresses duration, not a single working.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标展开的系列行动，常为宣传或军事行动；强调持续时间，而非单次运作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Latin noun of work plus a noun suffix: the doing of work, and then any piece of work that is done.
normal.cn: 拉丁「工作」名词加名词后缀：先指干活，再指所干的任一件事。

normal.en: One root yields the verb to run, the person who runs, the adjective for running order and the noun for joint work.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出表示运转的动词、表示操作者的名词、表示运转状态的形容词，以及表示合作的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: in operation, surgical operation, rescue operation, daily operations.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：在运转中、外科手术、救援行动、日常业务。

normal.en: Hospitals, armies and mathematics all call their own kind of work by this one name.
normal.cn: 医院、军队与数学都把自己那类工作用同一个名称来称呼。

normal.en: A factory is said to be in operation, and later the factory itself is called an operation.
normal.cn: 工厂被说成处于运转中，后来工厂本身也被称为一个经营单位。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose gears keep turning while nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的齿轮在无人注视时仍不停转动。

abstract.en: Picture a surgeon's hands as the only still thing in a room full of machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子机器都在动，只有外科医生的手是静的。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures that changes when one rule is applied.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字在施加一条规则后整体改变。

examples.en: The plant has been in operation since the river was dammed.
examples.cn: 这座工厂自河流筑坝以来一直在运转。

examples.en: The peacekeeping operation was extended for another six months.
examples.cn: 维和行动又延长了六个月。

examples.en: Division is the operation most often done wrong under time pressure.
examples.cn: 除法是时间紧迫时最容易算错的一种运算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oper（工作）+ ation（名词）」——在工作、在运转 → 运转、操作、手术、行动、运算

root: 拉丁语「工作」名词派生出「工作、施行」的动词，再加后缀构成「工作、运作」的名词；名词词根更早的来源无定论，相关词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of working: a machine runs, a hand makes it run, a surgeon works on a body, an army works on an objective, a company works every day, a rule works on numbers, a working enterprise is itself a unit, and any coordinated effort is one operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「工作」动作展开：机器运转、手使它运转、医生在身体上工作、军队对一个目标行动、公司每天运作、规则对数字起作用、运转中的企业本身成为一个单位，最后任何协同用力都算一次行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gears turning under a lamp while a hand rests on the switch that keeps them turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下齿轮转动，一只手按在使它们继续转动的开关上。

branches.en: RUNNING AND DRIVING: the working of a system and the act that keeps it working are one event seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 运转与驱动：系统的运转与使它运转的动作，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: ON A BODY: surgery is work performed on flesh with tools.
branches.cn: 施于身体：手术是用工具在血肉上所做的工作。

branches.en: ON AN AIM: a named military action and any coordinated effort are work organized toward one end.
branches.cn: 对准目标：有代号的军事行动与任何协同工作，都是朝一个目标组织起来的劳动。

branches.en: THE WORKING UNIT: a company's daily business and the enterprise itself are the same working seen as activity and as thing.
branches.cn: 运转单位：公司的日常业务与企业本身，是同一个运转被看作活动与看作实体。

branches.en: ON SYMBOLS: arithmetic applies the same notion of work to numbers.
branches.cn: 施于符号：算术把同一个「工作」观念用在数字上。

intro.en: Operation is a Latin noun of work: a root noun for a task and a verb for doing it, with a suffix that turns the doing into a name.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「工作」的拉丁名词：一个指任务的词根名词、一个指做这件事的动词，以及把「做」变成名称的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus and operari give operate, operator, operation and cooperation; the noun suffix marks the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「工作」的名词与动词衍生出运转、操作者与合作等词；名词后缀标记动作或其结果。

items.example: The root noun names the task itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词指任务本身。

items.example: The verb turns the task into activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把任务变成活动。

items.example: The suffix makes the activity a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把活动变成可计数的东西。

items.example: English keeps both the activity and its result.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼指动作与其结果。

items.example: The suffix is the same one that builds many nouns of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成许多表示过程的名词。

items.example: One verb covers machines, businesses and surgeons.
items.exampleCN: 一个动词兼指机器、企业与外科医生。

items.meaning: one who works a machine or business
items.meaningCN: 操作机器或经营业务的人
items.example: The agent suffix names the person at the controls.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指在控制台前的人。

items.example: The prefix makes the work shared.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使这份工作成为共享的。

items.meaningCN: 处于运转状态的；生效的
items.example: A rule becomes operative when it starts to apply.
items.exampleCN: 规则开始适用时便生效。

latinEntries.structure: operari, operatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 绩效评估；性能评测；表现评价
definition_en: a formal judgement of how well a person, a machine or an activity has done against agreed standards
core_image: 年终考评的会议室里，主管在评分表上逐项打分，旁边的投影显示着全年产出曲线
scene: 年终考评会上，主管对照评分表逐项记下每个人这一年的产出与协作情况。The annual performance evaluation compares each worker's output with agreed targets.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「对照既定目标判断工作成效的正式评估」（第 1 个义项：对员工年度工作成果的正式评定）；句意为年度绩效评估把每位员工的产出与商定目标作比较。图中可辨识物件：评分表、产出曲线、会议桌、签字笔。

pos.zh: 绩效评估（可数名词短语）
性能评测；表现评价（可数名词短语）

derivatives.zh: 表现不佳；业绩低于预期

senses.title: A formal judgement of a worker's year
senses.definition: the periodic review in which a manager rates an employee's results against set goals
senses.definitionCN: 主管对照既定目标，定期评定员工业绩的程序
senses.example: The annual performance evaluation compares each worker's output with agreed targets.
senses.exampleCN: 年度绩效评估把每位员工的产出与商定目标作比较。
senses.why: Performance here means how well someone carried out the job, and evaluation means fixing its worth, so the phrase is a judgement of work done.
senses.whyCN: 这里的前一个词指工作执行得如何，后一个词指判定其价值，因此这个短语就是对已完成工作的评判。

senses.title: A test of how well a machine works
senses.definition: a measured assessment of the speed, accuracy or efficiency of a device under stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在规定条件下对装置速度、精度或效率的测量评定
senses.example: A performance evaluation of the new pump showed a ten percent gain.
senses.exampleCN: 对新泵的性能评测显示效率提高了百分之十。
senses.why: Machines also perform, so the same phrase moved from people to equipment and now means a bench test.
senses.whyCN: 机器也在「表现」，因此同一短语从人转到设备，如今指台架测试。

senses.title: A review of whether a project met its aims
senses.definition: an assessment of a programme's delivery against its plan, often required by funders
senses.definitionCN: 对照计划评定某项目的交付情况，常由出资方要求
senses.example: The donors asked for a performance evaluation halfway through the project.
senses.exampleCN: 出资方要求在项目进行到一半时做一次执行评估。
senses.why: A project performs in the sense of delivering, so its mid-course review took the same name as a staff appraisal.
senses.whyCN: 项目在「交付」意义上也在表现，因此其中期评审与员工考核用了同一名称。

senses.title: An assessment of a student's demonstrated work
senses.definition: a judgement based on what a learner actually produces rather than on a single test score
senses.definitionCN: 依据学习者实际完成的成果而非单次考试分数作出的评定
senses.example: Teachers use a performance evaluation rubric rather than a single test score.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用表现评价量表，而不是只看一次考试分数。
senses.why: Education borrowed the phrase to separate what a student does from what a test measures, and a rubric makes the judgement explicit.
senses.whyCN: 教育借这个短语把学生实际做到的事与考试测到的东西分开，评分量表使这种判断明确可见。

senses.title: A review of an organization's results
senses.titleCN: 组织或子公司业绩评估
senses.definition: a formal judgement of how a division or subsidiary has performed over a period
senses.definitionCN: 对某部门或子公司在某一时期业绩的正式评定
senses.example: The board's performance evaluation of the subsidiary led to a sale.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会对该子公司的业绩评估最终导致将其出售。
senses.why: Whole units are judged by results too, so the phrase scales from one worker to an entire company.
senses.whyCN: 整个单位也按结果受评，因此这个短语可以从一名员工扩展到一整家公司。

senses.title: A benchmark of a model or algorithm
senses.definition: a measured comparison of a system's accuracy, speed or cost on a fixed set of tasks
senses.definitionCN: 在固定任务集上对系统准确率、速度或成本的测量比较
senses.example: The team ran a performance evaluation of three speech models on the same data.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在同一批数据上对三个语音模型做了性能评估。
senses.why: Software performs on tasks, so testing it against a fixed set became another performance evaluation.
senses.whyCN: 软件在任务上「表现」，因此在固定任务集上测试它，又成了一种性能评估。

senses.title: The measurement of actual language use
senses.definition: in linguistics, the study of real utterances rather than of the underlying knowledge that produces them
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中研究实际说出的话语，而非产生话语的底层知识
senses.example: A performance evaluation in linguistics looks at actual utterances rather than idealized knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学中的运用评估考察实际说出的话语，而非理想化的知识。
senses.why: The field separates competence from performance, and measuring the latter is literally evaluating how language is performed.
senses.whyCN: 该学科把语言能力与语言运用分开，测量后者字面上就是评估语言被运用的情形。

senses.title: A judgement of athletic execution
senses.definition: a technical review of how a movement was executed, often from video
senses.definitionCN: 对某一动作完成质量的技术性评审，常借助录像
senses.example: Coaches video each sprint for a performance evaluation of technique.
senses.exampleCN: 教练为每次冲刺录像，用来做技术表现评估。
senses.why: Sport performs before an audience, so the review of technique inherited the word from the stage as much as from the office.
senses.whyCN: 运动在观众面前「表现」，因此对技术的评审既承自办公室，也承自舞台。

intro.en: The phrase joins a verb of carrying something through to a noun of worth. Performance came through Old French from a verb meaning to complete; evaluation came from French and rests on a Latin verb meaning to be worth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示「把事做完」的动词与一个表示「价值」的名词连在一起。前者经古法语出自意为「完成」的动词；后者来自法语，底子是拉丁语中表示「有价值」的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Par- 'thoroughly' plus fournir 'to provide' produced parfournir 'to carry out to the end, to complete'. The origin of fournir is uncertain, possibly Germanic.
items.cn: par-「彻底」加 fournir「提供」构成 parfournir，意为「做到最后、完成」。fournir 的来源不确定，可能出自日耳曼语。

items.en: Valere meant 'to be strong, to be well, to be worth'. Its deeper origin is a reconstruction, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: valere 意为「强壮、健康、有价值」。其更深来源属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: French évaluer 'to fix the value of' was formed on value, and English evaluation entered in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语中表示「确定价值」的动词由「价值」构成，这个词于十九世纪进入英语。

items.en: Performance first meant the carrying out of a task or the giving of a play, and only later the measured efficiency of a machine.
items.cn: 这个词最初指任务的完成或戏剧的演出，后来才指机器的实测效率。

items.en: Personnel management joined the two words in the twentieth century, and the phrase spread to equipment, projects and models.
items.cn: 二十世纪人事管理把这两个词连在一起，此后该短语扩及设备、项目与模型。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that share one of the two words but judge a different thing; group two holds single words for judging worth or performance.
note.cn: 第一组是共用其中一个词、但评判对象不同的短语；第二组是表示评判价值或表现的单字词。

entries.definition: The human-resources term for the same staff review; appraisal stresses the interview and the rating form.
entries.definitionCN: 人力资源领域对同一种员工考核的叫法，更强调面谈与评分表。

entries.definition: A periodic look back at results; it may be informal and need not produce a score.
entries.definitionCN: 定期回顾成果，可以是非正式的，未必给出分数。

entries.definition: The continuing system of goals, feedback and rewards, of which one evaluation is a step.
entries.definitionCN: 目标、反馈与奖励的持续体系，单次评估只是其中一步。

entries.definition: A measure that signals how well something is going; it feeds an evaluation but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 指示运行状况的指标，供评估使用，但本身不是评估。

entries.definition: A judgement of the level or quality reached, often broader than one person's yearly results.
entries.definitionCN: 对达到的水平或质量所作判断，范围常比一名员工的年度成果更宽。

entries.definition: A judgement of value, used for property, staff and projects alike.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值的判定，可用于房产、员工与项目。

entries.definition: A formal check of accounts or compliance against rules, not of how well work was done.
entries.definitionCN: 对账目或合规情况的正式核查，而非评断工作做得好不好。

entries.definition: A standard against which results are compared; it supplies the yardstick rather than the verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 用来比较结果的标准，提供尺子而不给出结论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first word names how a task was carried out; the second names the act of fixing its worth.
normal.cn: 前一个词指任务执行得如何，后一个词指判定其价值的动作。

normal.en: One family runs perform, performance, performer and underperform; the other runs value, evaluate, evaluation and evaluator.
normal.cn: 一族是同出「执行」的词，另一族是同出「价值」的词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the setting: annual performance evaluation, evaluation criteria, evaluation report.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：年度绩效评估、评估标准、评估报告。

normal.en: The phrase moves from staff to pumps, projects, students, models and sprinters, because all of them perform.
normal.cn: 这个短语从员工转到泵、项目、学生、模型与短跑者，因为它们都在「表现」。

normal.en: An indicator is a number; an evaluation is a judgement made with that number.
normal.cn: 指标是一个数字；评估是用这个数字作出的判断。

abstract.en: Picture a form with boxes, and a pen that hesitates before the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张带格子的表格，笔在最后一格前停了一停。

abstract.en: Picture two runners and one stopwatch shared between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者和一只两人共用的秒表。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror that reports not what you look like but how far you have come.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，照出的不是你的样子，而是你走了多远。

examples.en: The union objected that the performance evaluation rewarded speed over safety.
examples.cn: 工会反对说，绩效评估奖励速度而轻视安全。

examples.en: A performance evaluation of the battery pack is due before winter.
examples.cn: 电池组的性能评测要在入冬前完成。

examples.en: Without a performance evaluation, the grant cannot be renewed.
examples.cn: 没有执行评估，这笔资助就无法续期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「performance（表现）+ evaluation（评估）」——看表现再打分 → 绩效评估、性能评测

root: 这个短语的前半经古法语出自意为「做到最后」的动词，由「彻底」前缀加「提供」动词构成，后者来源不确定；后半经法语出自「价值」，再上溯拉丁语表示「有价值、强壮」的动词，其更早词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of judging: a worker's year is rated, a machine is bench-tested, a project is reviewed, a student's work is scored, a subsidiary is judged, a model is benchmarked, actual language use is measured, and a movement is filmed and graded.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个评判动作展开：评员工一年、试机器性能、审项目交付、给学生成果打分、判子公司业绩、给模型做基准、测实际语言运用，最后给一个动作录像评分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ratings sheet on a meeting table, every row compared with a target written in the same column.
core.cn: 核心意象：会议桌上的一张评分表，每一行都与同一列写着的目标对照。

branches.en: JUDGING PEOPLE: a worker's year and a student's work are rated by what was actually produced.
branches.cn: 评判人：员工的一年与学生的成果，都按实际产出评定。

branches.en: JUDGING EXECUTION: a pump on a bench and a sprint on video are both measured for how well they ran.
branches.cn: 评判执行：台架上的泵与录像里的冲刺，都在测它们运行得多好。

branches.en: JUDGING A WHOLE EFFORT: a project and a subsidiary are assessed against a plan and a target.
branches.cn: 评判整体：项目与子公司都对照计划与目标受评。

branches.en: JUDGING A MODEL: a fixed task set turns performance into a number to compare.
branches.cn: 评判模型：固定任务集把表现变成一个可比较的数字。

branches.en: JUDGING USE: linguistics measures utterances rather than the knowledge behind them.
branches.cn: 评判运用：语言学测量说出的话语，而非话语背后的知识。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two histories: a French verb of completing a task and a Latin-rooted noun of worth, each with its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两段历史构成：一个法语来源、表示「完成任务」的动词，以及一个拉丁词根、表示「价值」的名词，各自带一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere gives value, evaluate, evaluation and valuable; the French verb behind perform gives performance and performer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「有价值」的动词衍生出价值与评估等词；表示「完成」的法语动词则衍生出表现与表演者。

items.example: The source verb is French, and its own origin is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 这个源动词出自法语，其本身来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks doing a thing to the end.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记把事做到最后。

items.meaning: to carry through to the end
items.example: Completion is the core of the first half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 「完成」是这个短语前半的核心。

items.meaning: to carry out, to do, to act
items.example: A task and a stage role are both carried out.
items.exampleCN: 任务与舞台角色都要被「做出来」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the name of its doing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成其「做」的名称。

items.meaning: to be strong, to be worth
items.example: Worth is strength in the older sense of the word.
items.exampleCN: 价值在较早的词义里就是力量。

items.example: The noun names what something is worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指某物值多少。

items.example: To evaluate is to put a figure on worth.
items.exampleCN: 评估就是给价值定一个数。

items.example: The suffix makes the judging a named process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把评判变成一个有名称的过程。

items.example: The agent suffix names the judge.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指作出评判的人。

latinEntries.meaning: to be strong, to be worth

definition_zh: 优化；使达到最佳状态；调优（参数、设置）
definition_en: to make something as effective, efficient or favourable as it can be, often by adjusting its parts
core_image: 工程师盯着一块显示能耗曲线的屏幕，反复微调旋钮，直到曲线落到最低处
scene: 工程师把一组参数在屏幕上反复调整，直到耗电量降到最低。The team spent a week trying to optimize the cooling cycle before the trial run.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「把某个过程调整到能达到的最好状态」（第 1 个义项：使效果、效率或条件尽可能好）；句意为团队花了一周时间设法把冷却循环调到最佳，然后才试运行。图中可辨识物件：能耗曲线、旋钮、控制屏、试运行记录表。

pos.zh: 调优；反复调整参数使达到最佳

senses.title: Make something as good as possible
senses.definition: to bring a process, design or arrangement to the best state it can reach
senses.definitionCN: 把流程、设计或安排引到它能达到的最好状态
senses.example: The team spent a week trying to optimize the cooling cycle before the trial run.
senses.exampleCN: 团队花了一周时间把冷却循环调到最佳，然后才试运行。
senses.why: The base is a Latin word for the best, so the verb means to move something toward its best state.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的底子是拉丁语中表示「最好」的词，因此动词的意思是使某物朝最好的状态移动。

senses.title: Tune settings for the best result
senses.definition: to adjust the settings of a device or program until the output is best for the chosen use
senses.definitionCN: 反复调整装置或程序的设置，直到输出对既定用途最有利
senses.example: She optimized the camera settings for low light.
senses.exampleCN: 她把相机设置调到最适合弱光的状态。
senses.why: Adjusting knobs one at a time is the practical form of moving toward the best, so tuning took the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 一个个拧旋钮，正是「朝最好移动」的实际做法，因此调参也用了这个动词。

senses.title: Find the best solution mathematically
senses.definition: to determine the arrangement that minimises cost or maximises a chosen measure
senses.definitionCN: 求出使成本最小或使某项指标最大的安排
senses.example: The algorithm optimizes the route across forty delivery points.
senses.exampleCN: 算法为跨越四十个配送点的路线求最优解。
senses.why: Optimisation in mathematics is the formal search for the best point, and the everyday verb borrowed that name.
senses.whyCN: 数学中的最优化就是形式化地寻找最优点，日常动词借用了这个名称。

senses.title: Improve compiled code
senses.definition: to rewrite a program during compilation so that it runs faster or uses less memory
senses.definitionCN: 在编译时改写程序，使其运行更快或占用内存更少
senses.example: The compiler optimizes loops that run millions of times.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器会优化要运行数百万次的循环。
senses.why: A compiler chooses the best instruction sequence it can from the same source, which is optimisation applied to code.
senses.whyCN: 编译器从同一份源码中选出它所能选的最好指令序列，这就是把最优化用在代码上。

senses.title: Allocate resources in the best way
senses.definition: to distribute money, staff or time so that the overall result is best
senses.definitionCN: 分配资金、人力或时间，使总体结果最好
senses.example: The city optimized bus frequencies to cut waiting time.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门优化了公交班次，以缩短候车时间。
senses.why: When several demands compete for one supply, the best distribution is what optimisation means in practice.
senses.whyCN: 当多种需求争一份供给时，最好的分配就是最优化在实践中的含义。

senses.title: Adapt something to a specific condition
senses.definition: to shape a design or a crop for one set of conditions rather than for general use
senses.definitionCN: 使设计或作物适配某一组条件，而非追求通用
senses.example: The crop was optimized for dry seasons rather than for yield.
senses.exampleCN: 这种作物是为旱季条件优化的，而不是为产量优化的。
senses.why: The best state depends on the conditions, so adapting to one environment is also moving toward the best for that environment.
senses.whyCN: 最好的状态取决于条件，因此适配某一环境也是朝该环境下的最好状态移动。

senses.title: Cut waste and raise efficiency
senses.definition: to remove avoidable loss from a system so that the same output costs less
senses.definitionCN: 去掉系统里可避免的损耗，使同样产出花费更少
senses.example: New insulation optimized fuel use in the kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 新的保温层优化了窑炉的燃料使用。
senses.why: Less waste is one face of the best state, so saving fuel counts as optimising the kiln.
senses.whyCN: 少浪费就是最好状态的一面，因此节省燃料也算把窑炉优化了。

senses.title: Tune for a target rather than for users
senses.titleCN: 为指标而非使用者调优
senses.definition: to adjust something so that a measured score improves, sometimes at the cost of real quality
senses.definitionCN: 为使某项测量分数提高而调整，有时牺牲真实质量
senses.example: The site was optimized for search engines rather than for readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站是为搜索引擎优化的，而不是为读者优化的。
senses.why: When the measure replaces the purpose, moving toward the best score can move away from the best result, which gives this critical sense.
senses.whyCN: 当指标取代了目的，朝最高分移动可能偏离最好结果，这就产生了这个带批评意味的义项。

intro.en: Optimize was coined in English on a Latin base: optimus 'best', the superlative of bonus 'good'. The word first belonged to philosophy and only later to engineering. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语中用拉丁语词根造出来的：拉丁语中表示「最好的」一词是「好」的最高级。它最初属哲学用语，后来才归入工程。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bonus meant 'good'. Its older form is usually reconstructed as duonus, and that earlier shape is a reconstruction rather than an attested word, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: bonus 意为「好」。其较早形式通常被重构为 duonus，而这个更早形状属重构而非书证，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Optimus, the superlative of bonus, meant 'best'. It supplies the whole idea of the verb: the best of a set.
items.cn: optimus 是 bonus 的最高级，意为「最好的」。动词的全部意思都来自它：一组之中最好的。

items.en: The neuter noun optimum meant 'the best thing', and English borrowed it later as a noun for the best point or value.
items.cn: 中性名词 optimum 意为「最好的东西」，英语后来借它作名词，指最佳点或最佳值。

items.en: The verb was formed in the nineteenth century with the suffix -ize, and it was first used in philosophical writing about being or acting at one's best.
items.cn: 这个动词在十九世纪加动词后缀构成，最初用于哲学写作，指处于或表现出最佳状态。

items.en: In the twentieth century the verb moved to machines, processes, mathematical search and compiler design, where the best state can be measured.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个动词转向机器、流程、数学搜索与编译器设计，因为在这些领域最佳状态可以被测量。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin superlative for best, plus one word from a different verb that looks close; group two holds verbs that also make something better.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「最好」最高级的词，外加一个形近但出处不同的词；第二组是同样表示「使更好」的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective for the best attainable state; it describes the result that the verb works toward.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可达到的最佳状态的形容词，描述动词所追求的结果。

entries.definition: The best point or value itself, often a temperature or a level found by testing.
entries.definitionCN: 指最佳点或最佳值本身，常为测出的温度或水平。

entries.definition: The habit of expecting the best outcome; it shares the root but names a mood, not a method.
entries.definitionCN: 指期待最好结果的习惯，同根但指情绪，而非方法。

entries.definition: From optare 'to choose', not from the word for best: a choice among alternatives.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 optare「选择」，而非「最好」一词：指备选方案中的一个。

entries.definition: To make something better in any degree; it claims no maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物有某种程度的改善，并不声称达到最大。

entries.definition: To make small successive changes that remove defects, often without a measurable target.
entries.definitionCN: 通过逐步的小改动去掉缺陷，常无可测量的目标。

entries.definition: To adjust a device by hand until it runs well; it is the practical half of the same work.
entries.definitionCN: 用手调整装置直到运行良好，是同一工作的实操那一半。

entries.definition: To simplify a process by cutting steps, which is one way of reaching a better state.
entries.definitionCN: 通过削减步骤简化流程，是达到更好状态的一种方式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin superlative for best plus a verb suffix: to move something toward the best it can be.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「最好」的最高级加动词后缀：使某物朝它能达到的最好状态移动。

normal.en: The family runs optimal, optimally, optimum, optimization, optimizer and suboptimal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示最佳的形容词、其副词、最佳点、优化、优化器与次优的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: optimize performance, optimize a process, optimize resource use, optimize for speed.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：优化性能、优化流程、优化资源使用、针对速度优化。

normal.en: Engineering optimizes a cycle, mathematics optimizes a route, computing optimizes a loop, a city optimizes a timetable.
normal.cn: 工程优化循环，数学优化路线，计算优化循环体，城市优化时刻表。

normal.en: The noun optimization names both the act of tuning and the best point reached.
normal.cn: 名词优化兼指调优的过程与所达到的最佳点。

abstract.en: Picture a marble rolling until it settles in the lowest dip of a bowl.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗弹珠滚动，最后停在碗底最低处。

abstract.en: Picture a hand turning a dial in tiny steps while a needle falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手一点点转动旋钮，指针随之下降。

abstract.en: Picture two roads to the same town, one of them shorter by a hundred paces.
abstract.cn: 想象通往同一小镇的两条路，其中一条短一百步。

examples.en: The plant optimized its water use and cut the bill by a third.
examples.cn: 工厂优化了用水，账单减少了三分之一。

examples.en: Engineers optimize for safety first and for cost second.
examples.cn: 工程师先为安全优化，其次才为成本优化。

examples.en: A model tuned to one market may be optimal nowhere else.
examples.cn: 针对一个市场调好的模型，在别处可能都达不到最佳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「optim（最好）+ ize（使……）」——使达到最好 → 优化、调优

root: 拉丁语中表示「最好的」一词是「好」的最高级，加动词后缀构成「使达到最好」；表示「好」的形容词更早的形状属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one motion: something is brought toward its best state, then that state is reached by tuning, by mathematical search, by rewriting code, by sharing resources, by fitting one condition, by cutting waste, and finally by chasing a score that may not be the real goal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物朝最好状态推动，再通过调参、数学搜索、改写代码、分配资源、适配某一条件、削减浪费去达到它，最后变成只追逐分数而未必是真正目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle falling toward the lowest mark on a dial as a hand makes smaller and smaller adjustments.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手做越来越小的调整，指针朝刻度最低处落下去。

branches.en: TOWARD THE BEST: making something as good as it can be and cutting waste are the same movement seen from two directions.
branches.cn: 朝最好：使某物尽可能好与削减浪费，是同一运动从两个方向看。

branches.en: ADJUSTING THE MACHINE: a hand on a dial and a compiler on a loop both trade one arrangement for a better one.
branches.cn: 调整机器：手拧旋钮与编译器改写循环，都是用更好的安排换掉原来的。

branches.en: CHOOSING THE BEST POINT: a route through forty stops and a city timetable are searches for the best arrangement.
branches.cn: 选择最优点：跨四十站的路线与城市时刻表，都是对最佳安排的搜寻。

branches.en: FIT ONE CONDITION: the best state is defined by the conditions, so adaptation is optimisation for that place.
branches.cn: 适配一种条件：最好状态由条件定义，因此适配就是针对该处的优化。

branches.en: CHASING THE SCORE: when the measure becomes the goal, moving to the best number can leave the best result behind.
branches.cn: 追逐分数：当指标变成目标，朝最好数字移动可能把最好结果抛在后面。

intro.en: Optimize is a modern English verb built on a Latin superlative, so its parts are a root meaning good, its highest degree, and a suffix that turns it into an action.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在拉丁语最高级之上的现代英语动词，其成分是一个意为「好」的词根、它的最高级，以及把形容词变成动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin bonus 'good' gives the superlative optimus 'best', hence optimal, optimum and optimize; the suffix -ize marks making or becoming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「好」的词给出最高级「最好」，由此衍生出表示最佳的形容词、最佳点与优化；动词后缀标记「使……」或「变为……」。

items.example: The root adjective is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根形容词是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The superlative supplies the direction of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 最高级提供动词的方向。

items.example: The noun names the endpoint rather than the motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指终点，而非运动本身。

items.example: The suffix turns a state into something one can work toward.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把一种状态变成可以努力追求的东西。

items.meaning: to make as good as possible
items.example: The verb is a nineteenth-century formation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是十九世纪形成的。

items.example: The adjective describes the endpoint.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述终点。

items.example: The adverb describes how the work is done.
items.exampleCN: 副词描述工作是怎样完成的。

items.meaning: the act or result of making best
items.example: The noun covers both tuning and the best point reached.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指调优过程与达到的最佳点。

items.example: The prefix marks a result that falls short.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标记未达最佳的结果。

definition_zh: 研究与开发；研发（指企业或机构为开发新技术、新产品而进行的系统性工作）
definition_en: the organized work of investigating questions and turning findings into new products, processes or services
core_image: 同一栋楼里，一层的人在做实验记录数据，另一层的人把图纸装成一台样机
scene: 实验室与企业共用同一栋楼，一边做基础研究，一边把成果做成样机。The company doubled its spending on research and development after the prototype worked.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「为开发新技术与新产品而进行的系统性研究与开发工作」（第 1 个义项：把探究与成果转化合并起来的整体活动）；句意为样机成功之后，公司把研发支出翻了一倍。图中可辨识物件：实验记录本、图纸、样机、两层之间的楼梯。

pos.zh: 研究与开发；研发（不可数名词短语）
研发部门；研发活动（可作可数用法）

senses.title: The combined work of inquiry and building
senses.titleCN: 探究与开发合并的整体工作
senses.definition: the whole activity in which questions are studied and the answers are turned into usable products or processes
senses.definitionCN: 既研究问题、又把答案转化成可用产品或工艺的整套活动
senses.example: The company doubled its spending on research and development after the prototype worked.
senses.exampleCN: 样机成功之后，公司把研发支出翻了一倍。
senses.why: Research looks for knowledge and development turns it into something usable, so the phrase names the two halves joined into one budget line.
senses.whyCN: 研究寻找知识，开发把它变成可用的东西，因此这个短语指把两半合成一条预算科目。

senses.title: The department that does this work
senses.definition: the organizational unit where this work is carried out, often called simply by the same phrase
senses.definitionCN: 承担这类工作的组织单位，常直接用同一短语称呼
senses.example: Research and development moved into the new wing last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 研发部门去年春天搬进了新配楼。
senses.why: A unit is named after its activity, so the office that carries out the work takes the name of the work.
senses.whyCN: 单位常以所做之事命名，因此执行这项工作的部门沿用了工作本身的名称。

senses.title: Basic science joined to engineering
senses.titleCN: 基础研究与应用工程的结合
senses.definition: the deliberate pairing of pure inquiry with the engineering needed to make it useful
senses.definitionCN: 把纯探究与使其变得有用所需的工程有意配对
senses.example: The programme joins basic science with engineering under one research and development budget.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目把基础科学与工程合在一条研发预算之下。
senses.why: The phrase covers both ends of the pipeline, which is why laboratories and workshops appear in the same account.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语覆盖整条链条的两端，因此实验室与车间出现在同一本账里。

senses.title: Work on a new product or process
senses.titleCN: 新产品或新工艺的开发
senses.definition: the part of the work aimed at producing a marketable good or a cheaper method
senses.definitionCN: 工作中以产出可售商品或更廉价方法为目标的那部分
senses.example: Most of the budget goes to research and development of a cheaper battery.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分预算用于更廉价电池的研发。
senses.why: Development is the stage where knowledge becomes a thing, so product work is the visible half of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 开发是知识变成实物的阶段，因此产品工作是这个短语里看得见的那一半。

senses.title: Public money spent on this work
senses.definition: government funding for the same activity, counted as a national or regional total
senses.definitionCN: 政府为同类活动提供的资金，按国家或地区总量统计
senses.example: Public spending on research and development rose faster than inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 公共研发支出增长快于通货膨胀。
senses.why: Governments buy the same work that firms buy, so the phrase appears in budgets and statistics as a spending category.
senses.whyCN: 政府购买的工作与企业购买的是同一种，因此这个短语作为支出科目出现在预算与统计中。

senses.title: Work that carries a drug to approval
senses.definition: the long sequence of testing that turns a compound into an approved treatment
senses.definitionCN: 把一种化合物变成获批疗法的漫长试验序列
senses.example: Research and development of the vaccine took eleven years.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗的研发用了十一年。
senses.why: In medicine the development half is trials and regulation, which makes the phrase the standard name for the whole pipeline.
senses.whyCN: 在医药领域，开发那一半是试验与审批，这使该短语成为整条流程的标准称呼。

senses.title: Spending measured against revenue
senses.titleCN: 研发强度（支出占收入的比例）
senses.definition: the ratio of such spending to sales, used to compare how hard firms or industries try
senses.definitionCN: 这类支出与销售额之比，用来比较企业或行业的投入力度
senses.example: The industry's research and development intensity is below its rival's.
senses.exampleCN: 该行业的研发强度低于其竞争对手。
senses.why: Once spending is counted, it can be divided by revenue, and that ratio became a standard measure under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 支出一旦可以计数，就能除以收入，这个比值便以同一名称成为标准指标。

senses.title: Joint work between organizations
senses.definition: an agreement under which two or more organizations share the work, the cost and the results
senses.definitionCN: 两家或多家机构分担工作、成本与成果的协议
senses.example: The two firms share a research and development agreement on sensors.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司就传感器签有研发合作协议。
senses.why: Because the work is expensive and specialised, it is often shared, and the phrase then names the collaboration itself.
senses.whyCN: 这类工作昂贵且专门，常被分摊，此时该短语指合作本身。

intro.en: The phrase joins two French-derived nouns. Research rests on a Latin verb of going round in search; development rests on a French verb of unwrapping whose origin is uncertain. The pair became a budget term in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个法语来源的名词组成。前半的底子是拉丁语中表示「四处寻找」的动词；后半的底子是法语中表示「解开包裹」的动词，其来源不确定。两者在二十世纪合为预算术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Circare, from circus 'circle', meant 'to go about, to search around'. The origin of circus is unsettled, so the deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: circare 出自 circus「圆圈」，意为「四处走、到处搜寻」。circus 的来源没有定论，故更深词根不确定。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus cerchier 'to search' produced recercher, 'to search closely', which English borrowed as research.
items.cn: re-「再次」加 cerchier「寻找」构成 recercher，意为「仔细搜寻」，英语借为这个词。

items.en: Des- 'un-' plus voloper 'to wrap' produced desvoloper, 'to unwrap, to unfold'. The origin of voloper is uncertain, possibly Germanic.
items.cn: des-「解除」加 voloper「包裹」构成 desvoloper，意为「解开、展开」。voloper 的来源不确定，可能出自日耳曼语。

items.en: English development first meant the unfolding of something already present, then the growth of an economy or a product.
items.cn: 这个词最初指把已有之物展开，后来指经济或产品的成长。

items.en: Industry and government joined the two nouns in the twentieth century, and the pair became a standard budget heading and a common abbreviation.
items.cn: 企业与政府在二十世纪把这两个名词连用，此后它成为标准预算科目，并产生了通用缩写。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that share one of the two nouns but carry out a different kind of work; group two holds nouns for the work of producing knowledge or things.
note.cn: 第一组是共用其中一个名词、但所做工作不同的短语；第二组是表示「产出知识或实物」这一工作的名词。

entries.definition: The compressed form of the same phrase, used in budgets, job titles and headlines where space is short.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语的压缩形式，用于预算、职位名称与标题等篇幅有限处。

entries.definition: Inquiry aimed at a known practical problem; it is the research half without the development stage.
entries.definitionCN: 针对已知实际问题的探究，只有研究那一半，没有开发阶段。

entries.definition: The work of turning a design into a sellable product, which is the development half on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 把设计变成可售产品的工作，即单独取出的开发那一半。

entries.definition: Study of buyers and demand; it shares the word research but has nothing to do with laboratories.
entries.definitionCN: 对买家与需求的研究，共用「研究」一词，但与实验室无关。

entries.definition: The introduction of something new into use; it begins where research and development ends.
entries.definitionCN: 把新事物引入使用，起点正是研发结束之处。

entries.definition: The first devising of something; it need not be developed, tested or sold.
entries.definitionCN: 首次想出某物，不必经过开发、测试或销售。

entries.definition: The disciplined design of working things; it overlaps with development but excludes the open inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 在约束条件下对可用物的严谨设计，与开发重叠，但不含开放式探究。

entries.definition: Inquiry into how things work with no product yet in view, which is the opposite end of the pipeline.
entries.definitionCN: 探究事物如何运作而尚无视产品，是整条链条的另一端。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One noun means searching closely again and again; the other means unwrapping what is folded, then letting it grow.
normal.cn: 一个名词指反复仔细搜寻；另一个指把折起的东西解开，再让它生长。

normal.en: The first family runs research, researcher and researching; the second runs develop, developer, development and developing.
normal.cn: 前一族是同出「研究」的名词与动词，后一族是同出「开发」的名词与动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: spending, budget, department, project, agreement.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：研发支出、研发预算、研发部门、研发项目、研发协议。

normal.en: The pair is one budget line, so a company can report a single figure for two very different kinds of work.
normal.cn: 两者合成一条预算科目，因此公司能为两类很不同的工作报出一个数字。

normal.en: The abbreviation appears wherever the full phrase would take too much room.
normal.cn: 缩写形式出现在全称太占地方的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a stair between two rooms, one full of notebooks and one full of tools.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间之间的一段楼梯，一间堆满笔记，一间堆满工具。

abstract.en: Picture a folded paper that is opened slowly until a machine appears on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折起的纸慢慢展开，纸上浮现出一台机器。

abstract.en: Picture a seed and a factory sharing one calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子与一座工厂共用同一份日历。

examples.en: The ministry counts research and development as one category in its budget.
examples.cn: 该部在预算中把研发作为一个科目统计。

examples.en: Half of research and development is failure that never reaches a report.
examples.cn: 研发中有一半是从未写进报告的失败。

examples.en: The two universities run a joint research and development centre for batteries.
examples.cn: 两所大学合办了一个电池研发中心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「research（反复搜寻）+ development（展开生长）」——先找知识再做成东西 → 研究与开发

root: 这个短语由两个法语来源的名词构成：前者底子是拉丁语「绕圈寻找」的动词，加「再次」前缀；后者底子是法语「解开包裹」的动词，加「解除」前缀，该动词来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pipeline: inquiry and building are joined, an office is named after the work, pure science meets engineering, a product appears, public money buys the same work, a drug runs the gauntlet of trials, spending becomes a ratio, and finally two organizations share the burden.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条流水线展开：探究与建造合并，部门以工作命名，纯科学遇上工程，产品出现，公共资金买同样的工作，药物走完试验关卡，支出变成一个比值，最后两家机构分担这份负担。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laboratory bench at one end of a building and a prototype on a trestle at the other, joined by a single corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼的一端是实验台，另一端是支架上的样机，中间由一条走廊相连。

chain: IT IS TURNED INTO A THING

branches.en: THE WHOLE PIPELINE: inquiry and building are funded and managed as one activity.
branches.cn: 整条流水线：探究与建造被当作一项活动来资助与管理。

branches.en: WHO DOES IT: the office named after the work and the agreement that shares it are two ways of organizing the same effort.
branches.cn: 由谁来做：以工作命名的部门与分摊工作的协议，是组织同一份努力的两种方式。

branches.en: BOTH ENDS MEET: pure science and engineering sit under one budget, which is the phrase's defining claim.
branches.cn: 两端相接：纯科学与工程同处一条预算，这正是该短语的定义性主张。

branches.en: MAKING SOMETHING USABLE: a cheaper battery and an approved vaccine are the same stage carried into different industries.
branches.cn: 做成可用之物：更廉价的电池与获批的疫苗，是同一阶段进入不同行业。

branches.en: COUNTING THE EFFORT: public spending and the ratio to sales are the same work turned into a number.
branches.cn: 计量投入：公共支出与占销售的比值，是同一份工作被变成数字。

intro.en: The phrase is two French nouns, each made of a prefix and a verb, so it can be read as four morphemes and then a third noun suffix on the second half.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个法语名词，各由一个前缀和一个动词构成，因此可以按四个语素读出，后半还多一个名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin circare 'to search around' gives research and the verb to search; French voloper 'to wrap' gives develop and development.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「四处寻找」的动词衍生出研究及其动词；法语表示「包裹」的动词衍生出开发及其名词。

items.example: The prefix marks repeated searching.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记反复搜寻。

items.example: The verb supplies the search itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「寻找」本身。

items.example: Repeated searching became the name of systematic inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 反复搜寻后来成为系统性探究的名称。

items.example: The prefix reverses the folding.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「包起来」反过来。

items.example: Its own origin is uncertain, possibly Germanic.
items.exampleCN: 其本身来源不确定，可能出自日耳曼语。

items.meaning: to unwrap, to unfold, to grow
items.example: Unwrapping became growth and then the making of a product.
items.exampleCN: 「解开」先引申为生长，再引申为做成产品。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb of unfolding into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把「展开」的动词变成名词。

items.meaning: the process of unfolding or growing
items.example: The noun covers both growth and the building of a product.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指成长与产品的做成。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person in the laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指实验室里的人。

definition_zh: 研发（研究与开发的缩写）；研发投入；研发部门
definition_en: the written abbreviation for research and development, used for the activity, its budget or the department that carries it out
core_image: 预算表上一行只写三个符号的科目，背后是一整层楼的实验室与样机
scene: 走廊尽头的门上只挂着两个字母与一个符号组成的缩写牌，里面一排排工位坐着写代码和做实验的人。Half the floor is given to R&D, and the other half to the sales team.
sceneCN: 句中的缩写指「研究与开发这一活动」（第 1 个义项：把探究与成果转化合并起来的整体工作）；句意为半层楼分给研发，另一半给销售团队。图中可辨识物件：门牌上的缩写、工位、实验台、销售样品架。

pos.zh: 研发（研究与开发的缩写，不可数）
研发部门；研发预算科目（可数或不可数）

senses.title: The compressed name of the activity
senses.definition: the short written form of research and development, used wherever the full phrase would be too long
senses.definitionCN: 研究与开发的书面短形式，用于全称过长之处
senses.example: R&D accounts for a fifth of the firm's budget.
senses.exampleCN: 研发占这家公司预算的五分之一。
senses.why: An abbreviation is the same name shortened, so the first sense is simply the activity under a compressed label.
senses.whyCN: 缩写就是同一个名称被缩短，因此第一个义项只是这项活动换了个压缩标签。

senses.title: The budget line in accounts
senses.titleCN: 会计与预算中的研发科目
senses.definition: a reporting line in which the cost of this work is recorded and audited
senses.definitionCN: 记录并审计这类工作成本的报表科目
senses.example: The auditor moved the pilot plant cost into R&D.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师把中试车间的成本挪进了研发科目。
senses.why: Once costs are booked, the abbreviation becomes a heading in accounts, with rules about what may be charged to it.
senses.whyCN: 成本一旦入账，这个缩写就成了账目中的一个科目，并有可否计入的规则。

senses.title: The department, in speech
senses.definition: the organizational unit that carries out the work, named by the abbreviation in everyday talk
senses.definitionCN: 承担这项工作的组织单位，日常口语里用缩写称呼
senses.example: R&D sits on the third floor.
senses.exampleCN: 研发部门在三楼。
senses.why: People shorten the name of a unit to the activity it performs, so the abbreviation stands for the department as well.
senses.whyCN: 人们把单位名称缩成它所做的事，因此这个缩写也用来指部门。

senses.title: A ratio used in statistics
senses.titleCN: 统计中的研发强度指标
senses.definition: spending on this work expressed as a share of sales or of national output
senses.definitionCN: 这类支出占销售额或国民产出的比例
senses.example: R&D as a share of sales fell for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 研发占销售额的比例连续三年下降。
senses.why: A counted cost can be divided by a base, and the ratio keeps the same short name in reports.
senses.whyCN: 可计数的成本能被除以基数，这个比值在报告里沿用同一短名。

senses.title: A joint project label
senses.definition: the tag given to a shared programme between firms, universities or governments
senses.definitionCN: 企业、大学或政府之间共享项目的标记
senses.example: The two universities signed an R&D pact on grid storage.
senses.exampleCN: 两所大学就电网储能签署了研发合作协议。
senses.why: Shared work needs a short tag in contracts and headlines, and the abbreviation supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 共享的工作在合同与标题里需要一个短标记，这个缩写正好提供。

senses.title: A tax and policy instrument
senses.titleCN: 税收与政策工具中的研发口径
senses.definition: the category used by governments to grant credits, grants or deductions for such work
senses.definitionCN: 政府为这类工作给予税收抵免、补助或扣除时所用的类别
senses.example: Small firms claimed the R&D credit for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业第一次申请了研发税收抵免。
senses.why: Policy must define what counts, and the abbreviation becomes the name of the qualifying category.
senses.whyCN: 政策必须界定什么算数，这个缩写便成了合格类别的名称。

senses.title: The output, not the input
senses.definition: the results that the work produces, such as patents, prototypes or publications
senses.definitionCN: 这项工作产出的结果，如专利、样机或论文
senses.example: Their R&D produced four patents and no product.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的研发产出了四项专利，却没有产品。
senses.why: A department's name can stand for what it produces, so the abbreviation sometimes means the output rather than the effort.
senses.whyCN: 部门名称可以代替它所产出之物，因此这个缩写有时指产出而非投入。

senses.title: A place where the work is done
senses.definition: a site, campus or building devoted to the activity
senses.definitionCN: 专门用于这项活动的场地、园区或建筑
senses.example: The R&D campus employs two thousand engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 研发园区雇用两千名工程师。
senses.why: A place is named after the work done in it, which is the same shortening seen in space rather than in budget.
senses.whyCN: 场地以在其中所做的工作命名，这是同一种缩短，只是发生在空间而非预算上。

intro.en: R&D is a written contraction of two French-derived nouns, with the ampersand standing for 'and'. The form appears in print in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个缩写取自两个法语来源名词的首字母，中间的符号代表「和」。这一写法在二十世纪见于印刷品。年代均为约数。

items.en: Circare 'to go about, search' is the base of the first half of the phrase. Its own root, tied to the word for a circle, is not fully settled.
items.cn: circare 意为「四处走、寻找」，是短语前半的底子。其词根与表示「圆圈」的词相关，但并未完全定论。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus cerchier 'to search' gave recercher, and English made research from it.
items.cn: re-「再次」加 cerchier「寻找」构成 recercher，英语由此得到这个词。

items.en: Des- 'un-' plus voloper 'to wrap' gave the verb of unwrapping behind the second half; the origin of voloper is uncertain.
items.cn: des-「解除」加 voloper「包裹」构成「解开」的动词，即短语后半的来源；voloper 的来源不确定。

items.en: The ampersand began as a written contraction of the Latin word for 'and', and English uses it in abbreviations of paired terms.
items.cn: 这个符号最初是拉丁语「和」一词的书写缩写，英语用它连接成对的词。

items.en: The abbreviation spread with industrial laboratories, wartime research budgets and later corporate reporting.
items.cn: 这个缩写在工业实验室、战时科研预算以及后来的企业报告中传播开来。

note.en: Group one holds written forms and compounds built on the abbreviation; group two holds words for the same work under other names.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在这个缩写之上的书写形式与复合词；第二组是用别的名称指同一工作的词。

entries.definition: The spelled-out phrase; it is the same referent in formal writing and legal text.
entries.definitionCN: 完整拼写的短语，在正式文书与法律文本中指同一对象。

entries.definition: The same abbreviation written with spaces, common where the symbol is inconvenient in text.
entries.definitionCN: 同一缩写的加空格写法，在符号不便排版的文本中常见。

entries.definition: The ratio of spending to sales, a compound that narrows the abbreviation to a single statistic.
entries.definitionCN: 支出占销售的比值，这个复合词把缩写收窄为一个统计量。

entries.definition: A single laboratory rather than the whole activity, which is the abbreviation used as a place name.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个实验室而非整项活动，是缩写被当作地点名称使用。

entries.definition: The bringing of something new into use, which follows the work the abbreviation names.
entries.definitionCN: 把新事物引入使用，发生在这个缩写所指工作之后。

entries.definition: The design of working things under constraints; it overlaps with the second half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 在约束下设计可用之物，与短语后半重叠。

entries.definition: Scientific work aimed at a known use, close to the first half but without the building stage.
entries.definitionCN: 面向已知用途的科学工作，接近前半但不含做成东西的阶段。

entries.definition: The work of turning a design into a sellable product, which the abbreviation covers only in part.
entries.definitionCN: 把设计变成可售产品的工作，缩写只覆盖其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The abbreviation takes the first letters of two nouns and joins them with the sign for 'and'.
normal.cn: 这个缩写取两个名词的首字母，用表示「和」的符号连接。

normal.en: The full phrase can always be restored, which is why formal writing avoids the short form.
normal.cn: 全称随时可以还原，因此正式文书避免使用短形式。

normal.en: Fixed compounds mark its uses: spending, budget, department, centre, credit, intensity.
normal.cn: 固定复合词标出用法：研发支出、研发预算、研发部门、研发中心、研发抵免、研发强度。

normal.en: The same three characters can mean the activity, the money, the office, the place or the results.
normal.cn: 同一串符号可以指活动、资金、部门、场地或成果。

normal.en: Statistical reports turn the abbreviation into a ratio, which is why it appears beside sales figures.
normal.cn: 统计报告把这个缩写变成一个比值，因此它常与销售数字并列出现。

abstract.en: Picture a budget row so short that it fits in one cell, while a whole floor of people works behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象预算表上一行短到只占一格，而它背后是一整层楼的人在干活。

abstract.en: Picture two doors with one shared nameplate between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门之间共用一块门牌。

abstract.en: Picture a patent certificate and an empty product shelf side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一张专利证书与一个空着的产品货架并排放着。

examples.en: The group spends more on R&D than on advertising.
examples.cn: 这个集团在研发上的花费超过广告。

examples.en: R&D asked for two more engineers before the deadline.
examples.cn: 研发部门要求在截止日期前再增加两名工程师。

examples.en: Investors read R&D as a sign of long-term confidence.
examples.cn: 投资者把研发投入看作长期信心的信号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 两个首字母加一个「和」的符号——研究与开发合称 → 研发

root: 两个法语来源名词首字母的书面缩写，中间符号原为拉丁语「和」一词的书写缩写；前半底子是拉丁语「四处寻找」的动词，后半底子是法语「解开包裹」的动词，后者来源不确定。
