sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one abbreviation: it names the work, then the money booked for it, the office that does it, the ratio it becomes, the contract that shares it, the tax rule that defines it, the patents it yields and the campus where it happens.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缩写展开：先指这项工作，再指为它入账的钱、做它的部门、它变成的比值、分摊它的合同、界定它的税则、它产出的专利，以及它发生的园区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three characters on a nameplate, with a laboratory bench on one side of the door and a budget sheet on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：门牌上三个符号，门的一侧是实验台，另一侧是预算表。

branches.en: THE WORK ITSELF: the compressed label still names the whole activity.
branches.cn: 工作本身：压缩后的标签仍指整项活动。

branches.en: MONEY AND RULE: the budget line and the tax category are the same figure seen by an accountant and by a government.
branches.cn: 钱与规则：预算科目与税收类别，是同一个数字被会计与政府分别看到。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PLACE: the department and the campus are the work given an address.
branches.cn: 人与地点：部门与园区，是这项工作有了地址。

branches.en: INPUT AND OUTPUT: the ratio measures what goes in, while the patents measure what comes out.
branches.cn: 投入与产出：比值计量投入，专利计量产出。

branches.en: SHARED WORK: a joint programme is the same effort written into a contract.
branches.cn: 共担的工作：联合项目就是同一份努力被写进合同。

intro.en: The abbreviation is built from the first letters of two nouns and a sign for 'and', so its parts are letters, a symbol and the two morphemes behind each half.
intro.cn: 这个缩写由两个名词的首字母与一个表示「和」的符号构成，因此其成分是字母、一个符号，以及每一半背后的两个语素。

latinIntro.en: Latin circare 'to search around' stands behind the first half; the French verb for wrapping stands behind the second; the ampersand began as a contraction of the Latin word for 'and'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「四处寻找」的动词是前半的底子；法语中表示「包裹」的动词是后半的底子；中间的符号原为拉丁语「和」一词的缩写。

items.example: The prefix marks repeated searching.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记反复搜寻。

items.example: The verb supplies the search.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「寻找」。

items.example: The first letter of this noun supplies the first character.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词的首字母提供第一个字符。

items.example: The prefix reverses the folding.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「包起来」反过来。

items.example: Its origin is uncertain, possibly Germanic.
items.exampleCN: 其来源不确定，可能出自日耳曼语。

items.example: The first letter of this noun supplies the last character.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词的首字母提供最后一个字符。

items.example: The sign joined the two nouns into one phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个符号把两个名词连成一个短语。

items.meaning: the first noun compressed to a letter
items.meaningCN: 第一个名词压缩为一个字母
items.example: Writing saves room by dropping the rest of the word.
items.exampleCN: 书写时省略词的其余部分以省地方。

items.meaning: the second noun compressed to a letter
items.meaningCN: 第二个名词压缩为一个字母
items.example: The pair reads as one term in budgets and headlines.
items.exampleCN: 两者在预算与标题里读作一个术语。

definition_zh: 技术的；技术上的；由技术引起的；技术先进的
definition_en: relating to technology, or brought about by machines, methods and applied knowledge
core_image: 车间里机械臂沿轨道移动，传感器把每一次位移变成屏幕上的数据点
scene: 车间里机械臂按程序移动，工程师把新装的传感器称为这一轮升级的关键。Technological change reached the workshop long before the office noticed.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「由技术发展带来的变化」（第 3 个义项：由机器、方法与应用知识引起的变化）；句意为技术变化早在办公室察觉之前就到了车间。图中可辨识物件：机械臂、轨道、传感器、数据屏。

pos.zh: 由技术引起的；技术先进的

senses.title: Relating to technology in general
senses.definition: connected with the tools, methods and applied knowledge a society uses
senses.definitionCN: 与社会所使用的工具、方法及应用知识有关
senses.example: Technological change reached the workshop long before the office noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 技术变化早在办公室察觉之前就到了车间。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun for the study of crafts to any subject it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把表示「技艺之学」的名词挂到它所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Advanced in equipment or method
senses.titleCN: 技术先进的；装备水平高的
senses.definition: equipped with or relying on a high level of machinery and method
senses.definitionCN: 装备或依赖高水平机器与方法的
senses.example: Their newest line is highly technological, with sensors at every station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最新的生产线技术含量很高，每个工位都有传感器。
senses.why: A plant that depends on many devices can be described by the adjective, so 'related to technology' shades into 'full of it'.
senses.whyCN: 依赖大量装置的工厂可以用这个形容词描述，于是「与技术有关」滑向「技术密集」。

senses.title: Caused by technology
senses.definition: brought about by machines or new methods rather than by nature or policy
senses.definitionCN: 由机器或新方法而非自然或政策造成的
senses.example: Technological unemployment follows when machines replace routine tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 当机器取代常规工作时，就会出现技术性失业。
senses.why: Once the adjective marks a cause, it can label effects that would not exist without the tools.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词标记原因时，它就能给那些离开工具便不会存在的后果贴标签。

senses.title: Pertaining to the limits of equipment
senses.definition: concerning what the available tools and methods can or cannot do
senses.definitionCN: 涉及现有工具与方法能做到或做不到什么
senses.example: The boundary is technological rather than legal.
senses.exampleCN: 这道界限是技术上的，而非法律上的。
senses.why: A limit set by tools is distinct from one set by law, and the adjective separates the two causes.
senses.whyCN: 工具造成的限制与法律造成的限制不同，这个形容词把两种原因分开。

senses.title: Demanding technical skill
senses.definition: requiring specialised method or skill rather than ordinary handling
senses.definitionCN: 需要专门方法或技艺，而非一般操作的
senses.example: Dyeing is the most technological step in the whole process.
senses.exampleCN: 染色是整个流程中技术性最强的一步。
senses.why: Where a step depends on exact methods, it is technological in the older sense of belonging to a craft.
senses.whyCN: 当一道步骤依赖精确方法时，它在「属于一门技艺」的较早意义上就是技术性的。

senses.title: Belonging to technical research
senses.definition: of the branch of work that develops tools and processes, as distinct from pure science
senses.definitionCN: 指开发工具与工艺的那类工作，与纯科学相区别
senses.example: Technological research and pure science answer different questions.
senses.exampleCN: 技术研究与纯科学回答的是不同的问题。
senses.why: Research aimed at making things work is separated from research aimed at understanding, and the adjective marks the first.
senses.whyCN: 以让东西能用为目标的研究，与以理解为目标的研究被区分开，这个形容词标记前者。

senses.title: Treating tools as the driver of history
senses.definition: in social theory, explaining change chiefly by the state of the tools
senses.definitionCN: 在社会理论中，主要以工具状况解释变化
senses.example: A technological view of history makes tools the driver of change.
senses.exampleCN: 一种技术论的历史观把工具当作变化的驱动力。
senses.why: When the adjective modifies a view rather than a thing, it claims that technology causes history.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词修饰的是一种观点而非物件时，它主张技术造成了历史。

senses.title: Pertaining to craft skill in restoration
senses.definition: concerning the manual and material knowledge needed to preserve or repair objects
senses.definitionCN: 涉及保存或修复物件所需的手工与材料知识
senses.example: The restoration needed technological skill as much as taste.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修复既需要品味，也同样需要工艺技术。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is craft, so repair work that depends on material knowledge is technological too.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的意思是技艺，因此依赖材料知识的修复工作同样属于技术层面。

intro.en: Technological joins a Greek noun for craft to a Greek suffix for study, and only in the modern period did it come to mean machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个希腊语中表示「技艺」的名词连到表示「学问」的后缀上，直到近代才用来指机器。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tekhne meant 'craft, skill, art', the knowledge of how to make something. Its earlier origin is reconstructed from a root often glossed 'to weave or fabricate', so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: tekhne 意为「技艺、技能、手艺」，即知道如何制作某物。其更早来源由常被解释为「编织、制作」的词根重构而来，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix -logia meant 'the study or account of', from logos 'word, reason, reckoning'.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia 意为「对……的论述或研究」，出自 logos「言词、理性、计算」。

items.en: Tekhnologia in Greek meant a systematic treatment of an art, not the art of machines.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekhno-logia 指对某门技艺的系统论述，而不是机器之术。

items.en: English technology first named a discourse on an art; the sense of practical arts and then machines developed later.
items.cn: 这个词最初指对一门技艺的论述；实用技艺义、再到机器义是后来发展的。

items.en: The adjective appeared in the nineteenth century, when industry began to be described in terms of applied knowledge and machinery.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现于十九世纪，当时人们开始用应用知识与机械来描述工业。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek root with different jobs, which are constantly confused; group two holds adjectives for advanced or machine-based work.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词根但分工不同的词，最易混淆；第二组是表示先进或机器化的形容词。

entries.tag: of a craft or a detail
entries.definition: Belonging to a particular craft or to the mechanical details of a subject; a technical fault is a small mechanical one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一门技艺或某一主题的机械细节；技术故障指小的机械问题。

entries.definition: A way of doing something skilfully; it is the craft itself, not the adjective of relation.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练做某事的方法，是手艺本身，而非表示关系的形容词。

entries.definition: The body of tools, methods and knowledge; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 工具、方法与知识的整体，形容词描述属于它的东西。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used of processes and states rather than of things.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，多用于过程与状态，而非物件。

entries.definition: Far along in development; it praises the level without naming the tools.
entries.definitionCN: 发展程度高，赞的是水平，不点明所用工具。

entries.definition: Working through numerical signals; it is narrower than technological and names a family of devices.
entries.definitionCN: 通过数字信号工作，比「技术的」窄，指一族装置。

entries.definition: Belonging to manufacturing on a large scale; a technological change need not be industrial.
entries.definitionCN: 属于大规模制造，技术变化未必是工业的。

entries.definition: Driven by physical parts; it covers only one part of what the adjective covers.
entries.definitionCN: 由物理部件驱动，只覆盖这个形容词所指的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Greek noun for craft plus a suffix for systematic study: the adjective describes whatever belongs to that study.
normal.cn: 希腊语「技艺」名词加表示系统学问的后缀：这个形容词描述属于这门学问的一切。

normal.en: The family runs technology, technologist, technically, technique and the adverb in -ly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括技术、技术专家、技术性地、技巧，以及加副后缀的形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the theme: change, development, innovation, advance, progress, breakthrough.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出主题：技术变革、技术发展、技术创新、技术进步、技术进展、技术突破。

normal.en: The root meant craft long before it meant machines, which is why a restorer's skill is also called technological.
normal.cn: 词根在指机器之前很久就指技艺，因此修复师的手艺也算技术层面。

normal.en: Keep the pair apart: technical points to a detail or a craft, technological points to the system of tools.
normal.cn: 要分清这一对：一个指向细节或某门手艺，另一个指向工具系统。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that once held a chisel and now holds a controller.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手，从前握着凿子，如今握着控制器。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every movement leaves a trace on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一间车间，每个动作都在屏幕上留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a timetable that changes because a machine changed, not because anyone voted.
abstract.cn: 想象一份时刻表因一台机器改变而改变，而不是因为有人投票。

examples.en: The gap between rich and poor regions is partly technological.
examples.cn: 富区与穷区之间的差距有一部分是技术上的。

examples.en: Technological advances in cooling made the desert farm possible.
examples.cn: 制冷技术的进步使沙漠农场成为可能。

examples.en: The report treats technological and legal barriers separately.
examples.cn: 报告把技术障碍与法律障碍分开处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「techno（技艺）+ logical（学问的）」——关于技艺之学的 → 技术的、技术引起的

root: 希腊语「技艺」名词加表示「系统学问」的后缀，再加形容词后缀；该名词的更早来源属重构形式，通常解释为「编织、制作」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: it points at tools in general, then at a high level of them, then at effects they cause, at limits they set, at skill they demand, at the research that improves them, at a theory that makes them the cause of history, and finally at the old craft sense of skilled hands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：先泛指工具，再指工具水平高，接着指工具造成的后果、设定的限制、要求的技艺、改进它们的研究、把它们当作历史动因的理论，最后回到「巧手之艺」的古老含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mechanical arm moving along a rail while a sensor turns each movement into a point of light on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：机械臂沿轨道移动，传感器把每一次位移变成屏幕上的一个光点。

branches.en: TOOLS IN GENERAL AND TOOLS IN PLENTY: the broad relation and the high level differ only in degree.
branches.cn: 泛指工具与工具密集：宽泛的关系与高水平只差程度。

branches.en: TOOLS AS CAUSE: an effect on employment and a theory of history both make the tool the reason.
branches.cn: 工具作为原因：对就业的影响与对历史的解释，都把工具当作理由。

branches.en: TOOLS AS LIMIT AND AS DEMAND: what equipment cannot do and what skill it requires are two faces of one constraint.
branches.cn: 工具作为限制与要求：设备做不到的事与它要求的技艺，是同一约束的两面。

branches.en: IMPROVING THE TOOLS: research aimed at better tools is the engine of the whole chain.
branches.cn: 改进工具：以更好的工具为目标的研究，是整条链条的发动机。

branches.en: THE OLD CRAFT: restoration returns the word to skilled hands and materials.
branches.cn: 古老的技艺：修复工作把这个词带回巧手与材料。

intro.en: Technological is built from a Greek noun of craft, a Greek suffix of study and a Latin-shaped adjective ending, so three layers meet in one word.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个希腊语「技艺」名词、一个表示「学问」的希腊后缀和一个拉丁形态的形容词词尾构成，因此三层来源汇于一词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin technologia carried the Greek compound into learned writing, and Late Latin technicus supplied the adjective of craft.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这一希腊复合词带入学术写作，晚期拉丁语则提供了表示「技艺的」形容词。

items.example: The root names the knowledge of how to make.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指「知道怎么做」的知识。

items.example: The suffix makes a systematic account of the craft.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使技艺成为系统论述的对象。

items.example: The combining form allows the noun to be joined to suffixes.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式使名词能接后缀。

items.meaning: a systematic treatment of an art
items.meaningCN: 对某门技艺的系统论述
items.example: The medieval noun still meant discourse, not machinery.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪名词仍指论述，而非机械。

items.meaning: the body of tools and methods
items.example: The modern noun narrowed to practical arts and then to machines.
items.exampleCN: 现代名词先收窄为实用技艺，再收窄为机器。

items.example: The ending makes the adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The adjective appeared when industry was described as applied knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词出现于人们用应用知识描述工业之时。

items.example: The adverb marks the point of view rather than the thing.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记看问题的角度，而非物件。

items.example: The person suffix names the practitioner.
items.exampleCN: 表示人的后缀指从业者。

latinEntries.structure: technicus (adj., Late Latin, from Greek tekhnikos)

definition_zh: 使自动化；用机器替代人工操作；自动控制
definition_en: to make a process or a task carry itself out by machine, with little or no human action
core_image: 一排机器自己上下料，传送带空转着把工件送到下一站，夜班只剩两名巡视工
scene: 车间里一排机器自己上下料，夜里只剩两名巡视工走来走去。The factory chose to automate the welding line rather than hire another shift.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「使某道工序由机器自行完成」（第 1 个义项：把原本靠人做的工序交给机器自动执行）；句意为工厂选择让焊接线自动化，而不是再招一个班次。图中可辨识物件：上下料机械手、传送带、夜班巡视灯、工件托盘。

pos.zh: 使自动化；把工序交给机器完成
自动控制；使设备自行运转

derivatives.zh: 自动装置；机械行事的人

senses.title: Make a process run itself
senses.definition: to convert a process so that machines carry out the steps that people used to perform
senses.definitionCN: 把原本由人完成的步骤改由机器执行
senses.example: The factory chose to automate the welding line rather than hire another shift.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂选择让焊接线自动化，而不是再招一个班次。
senses.why: The word is built on a Greek phrase meaning self-moving, so the verb means to give a process that self-moving power.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在希腊语「自行移动」的说法上，因此动词的意思是给某个过程这种自行运动的能耐。

senses.title: Control a device on a timer
senses.definition: to have a device start, stop or change by clock or sensor instead of by hand
senses.definitionCN: 让装置按时钟或传感器而非人手启停、改变
senses.example: A timer automates the pumps at night.
senses.exampleCN: 一只定时器在夜间自动控制水泵。
senses.why: A clock that acts in your place is the smallest form of self-moving, so a timer is enough to automate a pump.
senses.whyCN: 按时钟替你行动，是「自行运动」最小的形式，因此一只定时器就足以让水泵自动化。

senses.title: Replace jobs with machines
senses.definition: to remove human posts by giving their work to machines
senses.definitionCN: 把岗位上的工作交给机器，从而取消这些岗位
senses.example: Postal sorting was automated before the clerks retired.
senses.exampleCN: 邮局分拣在办事员退休之前就已自动化。
senses.why: When the work moves to a machine, the post that held it can disappear, which is the social face of the same change.
senses.whyCN: 工作移到机器上时，承载它的岗位就可能消失，这是同一变化的社会一面。

senses.title: Run a repeated task by script
senses.titleCN: 用脚本自动执行重复任务
senses.definition: to make a recurring task execute without being started by hand each time
senses.definitionCN: 让反复出现的任务不必每次手动启动就能执行
senses.example: She automated the weekly report with a short script.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个短脚本把周报自动生成。
senses.why: Repetition is what machines do best, so any task that recurs can be handed over and is said to be automated.
senses.whyCN: 重复是机器最擅长的事，因此任何反复出现的任务都能交出去，并被称为已自动化。

senses.title: Generate an output automatically
senses.definition: to have a document, record or message produced by a system as a by-product of another action
senses.definitionCN: 让文件、记录或消息作为另一动作的副产品由系统产生
senses.example: The system automates the invoice for every order.
senses.exampleCN: 系统为每一笔订单自动生成发票。
senses.why: If the trigger is a machine event, the output needs no author, so production itself counts as automation.
senses.whyCN: 若触发者是机器事件，产出就不需要作者，因此「生产」本身也算自动化。

senses.title: Run with nobody on site
senses.definition: to keep a site or service working through periods when no staff are present
senses.definitionCN: 在无人到场的时间段内维持场地或服务运转
senses.example: The depot was automated to run with no staff after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库被改造成午夜以后无人值守运行。
senses.why: The extreme case of replacing people is a place that needs none, which is why the verb covers unmanned operation.
senses.whyCN: 替代人的极端情形是完全不需要人的场所，因此这个动词也涵盖无人运行。

senses.title: Regulate a variable automatically
senses.definition: to keep a value within limits by a control loop that acts on measurements
senses.definitionCN: 通过依据测量值动作的控制回路把某个量维持在限度内
senses.example: Sensors automate the flow when pressure rises.
senses.exampleCN: 压力升高时，传感器自动调节流量。
senses.why: A control loop performs the judgement that an operator used to make, so regulation is automation of decision.
senses.whyCN: 控制回路执行了操作员原先所作的判断，因此调节是「决策」的自动化。

senses.title: Make people act like machines
senses.definition: to reduce a person's response to a fixed routine, so that it feels machine-like
senses.definitionCN: 使人的反应固定成一套程序，因而显得像机器
senses.example: The scripted lesson automated both teacher and class.
senses.exampleCN: 照本宣科的课堂把教师与学生都变得机械。
senses.why: If a routine can be handed to a machine, a person who follows it without judgement can be described by the same word, which gives this critical sense.
senses.whyCN: 既然一套流程能交给机器，那么不加判断照做的人也可以用同一个词描述，这就产生了这个带批评意味的义项。

intro.en: Automate comes from Greek automatos 'self-acting', a compound of autos 'self' and a second element whose origin is debated. The machine sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词出自希腊语表示「自行动作的」形容词，由意为「自身」的成分与一个来源有争议的第二成分构成。指机器的那层意思是近代才有的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Autos meant 'self, the same'. It is the clear half of the compound and supplies the idea of something acting on its own.
items.cn: autos 意为「自身、同一个」。它是这个复合词中清楚的一半，提供「自行活动」的意思。

items.en: Automatos meant 'self-moving, acting of itself'. The second element is disputed: one common reading links it to a root for thinking or eager desire, but that is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: automatos 意为「自行移动的、自己行动的」。第二个成分有争议：一种常见读法把它与表示「思考、欲求」的词根相连，但那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The noun automaton named a thing that moves by itself, and Greek writers used it of statues and self-opening doors.
items.cn: 名词 automaton 指自行移动之物，希腊作家用它指神像与自行开启的门。

items.en: French automate carried the noun into modern European languages in the seventeenth century, still for a self-moving device.
items.cn: 法语 automate 在十七世纪把这个名词带入近代欧洲语言，仍指自行移动的装置。

items.en: The English verb automate appeared in the eighteenth century, and the noun automation in the twentieth, when factories began to hand whole sequences to machines.
items.cn: 英语中表示「使自动化」的动词出现于十八世纪，其名词出现于二十世纪，当时工厂开始把整段工序交给机器。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same Greek compound with different grammatical jobs; group two holds verbs for making work less dependent on people.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊复合词、但词类与用法不同的词；第二组是表示「让工作少依赖人」的动词。

entries.definition: Describing a device or action that works by itself; it states the property that the verb creates.
entries.definitionCN: 描述自行工作的装置或动作，说明动词所造成的那种性质。

entries.definition: The changeover to machines, or the state of being machine-run; it is the noun of the whole movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指改由机器完成的转变或机器运行的状态，是整场变化的名词。

entries.definition: A self-moving machine or a person acting like one; it names the object, not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指自行移动的装置或像机器一样行动的人，指物件而非动作。

entries.definition: Greek 'self' joined to a Latin adjective for moving, but the compound means a carriage that moves itself, not a method.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「自身」加拉丁语表示「移动」的形容词，但这个复合词指自行移动的车，不是一种方法。

entries.definition: To equip work with machines; it stresses the hardware rather than the self-acting control.
entries.definitionCN: 给工作配上机器，强调硬件，而非自行控制。

entries.definition: To hand work to computers; it names one family of machines rather than the general change.
entries.definitionCN: 把工作交给计算机，指某一族机器，而非总体变化。

entries.definition: To simplify a process by cutting steps; it may still leave every step to people.
entries.definitionCN: 通过削减步骤简化流程，每一步仍可能由人完成。

entries.definition: To convert material into numerical form; it says nothing about who or what then acts on it.
entries.definitionCN: 把材料转成数字形式，并不说明之后由谁或什么来处理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek 'self' plus a second element: something that moves itself is the image behind the verb.
normal.cn: 希腊语「自身」加第二成分：自行移动之物，就是这个动词背后的意象。

normal.en: The family runs automation, automatic, automatically, automated and automaton.
normal.cn: 同族词包括自动化、自动的、自动地、自动化的与自动装置。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the setting: automate a process, automate production, fully automate, automate the line.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：使流程自动化、使生产自动化、实现全自动化、使生产线自动化。

normal.en: A timer, a script, a sensor loop and a whole factory are four sizes of the same handover.
normal.cn: 定时器、脚本、传感回路与整座工厂，是同一交棒的四种规模。

normal.en: When the handover is complete, a place can run all night with nobody inside.
normal.cn: 交棒彻底之后，一个场所可以整夜无人运行。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that picks up the tool as soon as the last worker puts it down.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一名工人刚放下工具，机器就把它拿了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that does the night shift alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟独自值夜班。

abstract.en: Picture a person reading a script so exactly that the voice sounds recorded.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人照着稿子读得极准，声音听起来像录好的。

examples.en: Small firms automate the tasks that eat their evenings.
examples.cn: 小企业把吃掉他们夜晚的那些任务自动化。

examples.en: The mill automated sorting and moved twelve workers to maintenance.
examples.cn: 工厂把分拣自动化，把十二名工人转到维护岗位。

examples.en: You cannot automate a judgement that nobody has written down.
examples.cn: 没人写下来的判断，无法自动化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「auto（自己）+ mate（动起来）」——让它自己动 → 使自动化、自动控制

root: 希腊语「自身」加一个有争议的第二成分构成「自行动作的」，再加动词后缀；第二成分的来源仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: a process is given to machines, a timer takes over a pump, a post disappears, a script repeats a task, a system issues a document, a site runs empty, a loop regulates a value, and finally a person is reduced to following a routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交棒展开：工序交给机器、定时器接管水泵、岗位消失、脚本重复任务、系统自动出单、场地无人运行、回路调节数值，最后连人也被压缩成照流程行事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of machines loading and unloading themselves while two night guards walk past with nothing to do.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排机器自己上下料，两名夜班巡视工无事可做地走过。

branches.en: HANDOVER: a whole process and a repeated task are the same transfer of action from hand to machine.
branches.cn: 交棒：整道工序与反复出现的任务，都是动作从手转到机器的同一种转移。

branches.en: SELF-ACTING CONTROL: a timer and a sensor loop both decide in place of a person.
branches.cn: 自行控制：定时器与传感回路都在替人作决定。

branches.en: WITHOUT PEOPLE: a lost post and an empty night shift are the same absence seen from the payroll and from the floor.
branches.cn: 没有人：消失的岗位与空掉的夜班，是同一缺席从工资册与车间两处看到。

branches.en: OUTPUT WITHOUT AN AUTHOR: an invoice made by the system has no hand behind it.
branches.cn: 无作者的产出：系统生成的发票背后没有一只手。

branches.en: THE PERSON AS ROUTINE: when a human follows the script without judgement, the machine's shape appears in the person.
branches.cn: 人成为流程：当人不加判断照稿行事，机器的形状便出现在人身上。

intro.en: Automate is a Greek compound plus an English verb ending: a word for self, a second element, a noun for a self-moving thing, and a suffix that turns it into an action.
intro.cn: 这是一个希腊复合词加英语动词词尾：一个表示「自身」的词、一个第二成分、一个表示自行移动之物的名词，以及把名词变成动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin and has no Latin relative; it entered modern languages through French, and English added the verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词出自希腊语，在拉丁语中没有同族词；它经法语进入近代语言，英语再加上动词词尾。

items.example: The first element supplies the idea of acting alone.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分提供「独自行动」的意思。

items.example: Its origin is debated, so no single root should be asserted.
items.exampleCN: 其来源有争议，不应断言某单一词根。

items.example: The adjective describes what happens without an outside hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述没有外手介入而发生的事。

items.example: The noun turned the adjective into a thing one could point at.
items.exampleCN: 名词把形容词变成可指认的东西。

items.example: The verb applies the old adjective to modern work.
items.exampleCN: 动词把这个古老的形容词用到现代工作上。

items.example: The ending supplies the action, not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾提供动作，而非词义。

items.example: The adjective names the property the verb creates.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指动词所造成的那种性质。

items.example: The noun appeared with the factory systems of the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词随二十世纪的工厂系统出现。

items.example: The participle doubles as an adjective for a finished line.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词兼作形容词，指已完成自动化的产线。

definition_zh: 制造业；制造过程；制造业的
definition_en: the business and process of making goods in quantity from raw materials, usually in factories
core_image: 钢卷沿辊道送进压机，压成车身侧板，火花顺着传送带一路落下
scene: 厂房里钢卷被压成车身侧板，火花沿着传送带一路闪烁。Manufacturing employs more people in this valley than farming does.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「以工厂批量生产商品的整个行业与活动」（第 1 个义项：把原料加工成成品的经济部门）；句意为在这个河谷里，制造业雇用的人比农业多。图中可辨识物件：钢卷、压机、车身侧板、火花与传送带。

pos.zh: 制造业；制造过程（不可数）

senses.title: The sector as a whole
senses.definition: the branch of the economy that makes goods in factories
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里制造商品的那一经济部门
senses.example: Manufacturing employs more people in this valley than farming does.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个河谷里，制造业雇用的人比农业多。
senses.why: The activity is named with a noun of process, and a whole sector takes the name of its characteristic activity.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动用表示过程的名词命名，整个部门便以它最具代表性的活动为名。

senses.title: The act of making goods
senses.definition: the process by which raw materials become finished goods
senses.definitionCN: 原料变成成品的过程
senses.example: Manufacturing of the wing takes eleven hours per unit.
senses.exampleCN: 每件机翼的制造需要十一小时。
senses.why: The noun of process names the doing itself, which is why it can be timed per unit.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示过程的名词指「做」本身，因此可以按件计时。

senses.title: The stage after design
senses.titleCN: 制造环节（相对于设计与销售）
senses.definition: the stage of production, as distinct from design, marketing or service
senses.definitionCN: 生产阶段，与设计、营销或服务相区别
senses.example: Design is done here, but manufacturing happens overseas.
senses.exampleCN: 设计在这里做，制造则在海外。
senses.why: A long chain of work is divided into stages, and the stage that turns drawings into objects takes this name.
senses.whyCN: 漫长的工作链被分成阶段，把图纸变成实物的那一阶段取了这个名称。

senses.title: Factory production as opposed to craft
senses.titleCN: 工业制造（与手工业相对）
senses.definition: machine-based production in quantity, as opposed to making by hand
senses.definitionCN: 以机器批量生产，与手工制作相对
senses.example: Cheap manufacturing replaced the village workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的工业制造取代了村里的作坊。
senses.why: The word entered English for goods made by hand, then shifted to the factory system that replaced handwork.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指手工制品，后来转向取代手工的工厂体系。

senses.title: The methods used to make things
senses.definition: the organised methods, such as lean production, by which goods are made
senses.definitionCN: 制造商品所用的有组织方法，如精益生产
senses.example: Lean manufacturing cut waste at every station.
senses.exampleCN: 精益制造削减了每个工位的浪费。
senses.why: Once the activity is studied, its methods are also called by the name, with adjectives to mark the variant.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动被研究之后，其方法也用同一名称称呼，再加形容词标出变体。

senses.title: The measured output of factories
senses.definition: the volume of goods produced, reported as an economic figure
senses.definitionCN: 所生产商品的数量，作为经济数字发布
senses.example: Manufacturing rose for a fourth quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 制造业产出连续第四个季度上升。
senses.why: Statistical offices count the activity and report its size, so the same noun becomes a number in the news.
senses.whyCN: 统计部门计量这项活动并报告其规模，因此同一名词在新闻里变成一个数字。

senses.title: Factory jobs taken together
senses.definition: employment in factories, treated as one block in labour statistics
senses.definitionCN: 工厂中的就业，在劳动力统计中被当作一整块
senses.example: Manufacturing shed two thousand jobs in the county.
senses.exampleCN: 该县制造业减少了二千个岗位。
senses.why: Jobs follow the sector, so the sector's name also stands for the people it employs.
senses.whyCN: 岗位跟着部门走，因此部门名称也代表它所雇用的人。

senses.title: Used as a modifier
senses.definition: placed before another noun to mark the part of the economy concerned
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，标出所涉的经济部分
senses.example: The manufacturing sector asked for cheaper power.
senses.exampleCN: 制造业部门要求更便宜的电价。
senses.why: A noun used before another noun turns into a description, which is how the word works as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 名词放在另一名词前就成了描述语，这个词作形容词时正是如此。

intro.en: Manufacturing is the noun of process from a French-derived verb whose Latin base means 'made by hand'. Its sense moved from handwork to factory work. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这是一个法语来源动词的过程名词，其拉丁底子意为「用手做成」。词义从手工制品转向工厂生产。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand'. Its deeper root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」。其更深词根属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do'. Its pre-Latin root is also a reconstruction.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、制作」。其在拉丁语之前的词根同样属重构形式。

items.en: The phrase manu factum meant 'made by hand', and it named work done with skill rather than by nature.
items.cn: 短语 manu factum 意为「用手做成」，指凭技艺而非天然生成之物。

items.en: French manufacture turned the phrase into a noun in the seventeenth century, and English borrowed it for things made by hand.
items.cn: 法语 manufacture 在十七世纪把这个短语变成名词，英语借它指手工制品。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the same noun moved to machine production in factories, and the process noun took the sector with it.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，同一名词转向工厂里的机器生产，过程名词也随之带上了整个部门的意思。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb in different grammatical roles; group two holds nouns for making goods.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词在不同语法角色下的形式；第二组是表示「制造商品」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb for making goods, and as a noun either the act or the products; it does not name the industry.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造商品的动词，作名词时指动作或产品，但不指整个行业。

entries.definition: The company that carries out the work, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指从事这项工作的公司。

entries.definition: Made in a factory, or invented rather than true; the participle carries both senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指工厂制成的，也指捏造而非真实的，两种意思都在这个分词里。

entries.tag: an old word for a factory
entries.definition: A nineteenth-century word for a factory building, now rare and historical.
entries.definitionCN: 十九世纪指工厂建筑的词，现已罕用，属历史词。

entries.definition: The making of goods or services of any kind, including farming and mining.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指商品或服务的生产，包括农业与采矿。

entries.definition: The branch of the economy, which may include extraction as well as making.
entries.definitionCN: 指经济部门，可能既包括采掘也包括制造。

entries.definition: The assembly of a structure from prepared parts, often on site.
entries.definitionCN: 用预制部件组装结构，常在现场进行。

entries.definition: The stage where components are joined, one part of manufacturing rather than the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把零件接合起来的阶段，是制造的一部分，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin phrase for 'made by hand' became a French noun, and English added a process ending to it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「用手做成」的说法变成法语名词，英语再给它加过程后缀。

normal.en: The family runs manufacture, manufacturer, manufactured and the adjective for what can be made.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造、制造商、制成的，以及表示「可制造的」形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: sector, industry, process, plant, costs, lean production.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：制造业部门、制造业、制造过程、制造厂、制造成本、精益制造。

normal.en: The word began as praise for handwork and ended as the name of the system that replaced it.
normal.cn: 这个词起初是对手工的赞许，最后成了取代手工的那套体系的名字。

normal.en: Governments report it as a number, and unions speak of it as jobs, but both mean the same factories.
normal.cn: 政府把它报成一个数字，工会把它说成岗位，但两者都指同一批工厂。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of steel that becomes a curve without anyone touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张钢板在无人触碰的情况下变成一个曲面。

abstract.en: Picture a village of workshops replaced overnight by one long shed.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间，一村作坊被一座长厂房取代。

abstract.en: Picture a number in a newspaper standing for thousands of dinner tables.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸上的一个数字，背后是成千上万张饭桌。

examples.en: Manufacturing moved inland as coastal rents rose.
examples.cn: 沿海租金上涨，制造业迁往内陆。

examples.en: The country wants to move from manufacturing to design.
examples.cn: 这个国家想从制造转向设计。

examples.en: Manufacturing output fell while services grew.
examples.cn: 制造业产出下降，而服务业增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「manu（手）+ fact（做）+ ing（过程）」——用手做出来的过程 → 制造、制造业

root: 拉丁语中表示「手」的名词与表示「做」的动词构成「用手做成」的短语，经法语变成名词，再加过程后缀；两个词根更早的来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one workshop: an industry is named after its activity, the activity is timed per unit, the stage is placed after design, machine work replaces handwork, the methods are studied and named, output becomes a statistic, jobs become a block, and the word finally works as a modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一间厂房展开：行业以活动得名、活动按件计时、环节排在设计的后头、机器取代手工、方法被研究并命名、产出变成统计数字、岗位成为一整块，最后这个词还用作定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coil of steel passing under a press and leaving as a curved panel, with sparks falling along the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷钢从压机下经过，出来时已成弯曲的板件，火花沿产线落下。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND SECTOR: the industry and the jobs inside it are one block of work counted two ways.
branches.cn: 人与部门：行业与其中的岗位，是同一块工作被两种方式计数。

branches.en: THE STAGE OF MAKING: the timed process and the stage after design are the same link in a longer chain.
branches.cn: 制造环节：可计时的过程与设计之后的阶段，是长链上的同一环。

branches.en: FROM HAND TO METHOD: machine production replaces the workshop, and then its methods are studied and named.
branches.cn: 从手到方法：机器生产取代作坊，随后其方法被研究并命名。

branches.en: OUTPUT AS A FIGURE: production becomes a number in the news.
branches.cn: 产出作为数字：生产变成新闻里的一个数字。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: the same noun placed before another word marks which part of the economy is meant.
branches.cn: 定语用法：同一名词放在另一词前，标出所指的是经济中的哪一部分。

intro.en: Manufacturing is a Latin phrase compressed into a French noun and then given an English process ending, so its parts are a word for hand, a verb for making and a suffix for the ongoing act.
intro.cn: 这是一个被压缩成法语名词的拉丁短语，再加英语过程后缀，因此其成分是一个表示「手」的词、一个表示「做」的动词，以及表示持续动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual and manage; facere gives factory and fabrication; the two meet in the phrase for made by hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「手」的词衍生出手动的与经营等词；表示「做」的动词衍生出工厂与制作等词；两者在「用手做成」的短语中相遇。

items.example: The root noun supplies the hand that holds the tool.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词提供握工具的那只手。

items.structure: facere, feci, factum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the making.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「制作」。

items.example: The phrase is the seed of the whole noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是整个名词的种子。

items.example: French compressed the phrase into one noun.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语压缩成一个名词。

items.structure: -ing (English noun suffix for an action or process)
items.example: The suffix names the activity rather than the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指活动，而非物件。

items.example: The agent suffix names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指施动者。

items.example: The participle also came to mean invented, since both are made.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词也引申为捏造的，因为两者都是「做出来的」。

items.example: The suffix marks feasibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记可行性。

definition_en: a company or person that makes goods from raw materials, especially in large quantities
core_image: 展会现场，一家工厂的展台上摆着自家生产的电机，名片上只印着工厂的名字
scene: 展会现场，一家工厂的展台上摆着自家生产的电机，名片上只印着工厂名。The manufacturer recalled twelve thousand units after a fault appeared in the field.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「生产这些商品的工厂或公司」（第 1 个义项：以原料批量生产商品的企业）；句意为现场出现故障后，制造商召回了十二万台产品。图中可辨识物件：展台、电机、名片、召回通知单。

pos.zh: 厂商；品牌所有者（相对零售商）

senses.title: A firm that makes goods
senses.titleCN: 制造商品的工厂或公司
senses.definition: a business that turns raw materials or parts into finished products
senses.definitionCN: 把原料或零件变成成品的企业
senses.example: The manufacturer recalled twelve thousand units after a fault appeared in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 现场出现故障后，制造商召回了十二万台产品。
senses.why: The agent suffix marks the doer of the verb, so the maker of goods is simply the one who manufactures.
senses.whyCN: 施动后缀标记动作的执行者，因此生产商品者就是执行「制造」的那一方。

senses.title: The brand owner, as against the shop
senses.titleCN: 与零售商相对的品牌厂商
senses.definition: the party responsible for the product's design and warranty, in contrast to the retailer
senses.definitionCN: 对产品设计与保修负责、与零售商相对的一方
senses.example: Retailers pass warranty claims back to the manufacturer.
senses.exampleCN: 零售商把保修索赔转回给厂商。
senses.why: Liability and warranty follow the maker rather than the seller, which fixes this legal-commercial sense.
senses.whyCN: 责任与保修跟着生产者而不是销售者，这固定了这层法律与商业含义。

senses.title: A maker of machinery
senses.definition: a firm that builds machines or equipment for other businesses
senses.definitionCN: 为其他企业建造机器或设备的企业
senses.example: The press manufacturer sends an engineer for every installation.
senses.exampleCN: 压机制造商每次安装都会派一名工程师。
senses.why: Industrial buyers speak of the firm that built the machine as its manufacturer, even when it makes nothing else.
senses.whyCN: 工业买家把造这台机器的企业称为它的制造商，即使它不做别的产品。

senses.title: A car maker
senses.definition: a company that assembles vehicles and sells them under its own name
senses.definitionCN: 组装车辆并以自己名义出售的公司
senses.example: Three car manufacturers share one battery plant.
senses.exampleCN: 三家汽车制造商共用一座电池工厂。
senses.why: In vehicles the assembler is treated as the maker even though most parts come from elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 在汽车业，即使大部分零件来自别处，组装者仍被视为制造者。

senses.title: A drug maker
senses.definition: a company that produces medicines and holds the licence for them
senses.definitionCN: 生产药品并持有相关许可的公司
senses.example: The drug manufacturer filed for approval in two markets.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药品生产商在两个市场申请了批准。
senses.why: Regulated products need a named responsible firm, and that firm is called the manufacturer in law.
senses.whyCN: 受管制产品需要一个具名的责任企业，法律上这家企业就称为制造商。

senses.title: A contract maker for another brand
senses.titleCN: 为他人品牌代工的生产商
senses.definition: a firm that builds goods to another company's specification and brand
senses.definitionCN: 按另一家公司的规格与品牌生产商品的企业
senses.example: As an original equipment manufacturer, it builds parts to a client's drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 作为原始设备制造商，它按客户的图纸生产零件。
senses.why: When design and brand belong to one firm and production to another, the producer is still the manufacturer of record.
senses.whyCN: 当设计与品牌属一家、生产属另一家时，生产方仍是名义上的制造商。

senses.title: An employer in wage talks
senses.titleCN: 劳资语境中的制造企业
senses.definition: factory owners taken together as the employing side in negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 在谈判中被当作雇主一方的工厂所有者整体
senses.example: The manufacturers and the union reached a wage deal.
senses.exampleCN: 制造企业与工会达成了工资协议。
senses.why: In labour disputes a whole group of firms is addressed as one party, and the trade name stands for the employers.
senses.whyCN: 在劳资争议中，一群企业被当作一方来对话，行业称呼便代表雇主。

senses.title: The responsible party in product law
senses.definition: the party legally answerable for a defect in a product, whatever the chain of sale
senses.definitionCN: 不论销售链条如何，对产品缺陷负法律责任的一方
senses.example: Liability falls on the manufacturer, not the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 责任落在制造商身上，而不是店铺。
senses.why: Product liability law needs one identifiable party at the origin, and that party is the manufacturer.
senses.whyCN: 产品责任法需要在源头有一个可辨认的责任方，这个责任方就是制造商。

intro.en: Manufacturer is the maker-noun of a French-derived verb, with an English agent suffix added. The Latin base means 'made by hand'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这是一个法语来源动词的施动名词，加上了英语表示「做者」的后缀。其拉丁底子意为「用手做成」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus 'hand' supplies the first half; its deeper root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: manus「手」提供前半；其更深词根属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: Facere 'to make' supplies the second half, and its pre-Latin root is also reconstructed.
items.cn: facere「制作」提供后半，其在拉丁语之前的词根同样属重构形式。

items.en: The phrase meant 'made by hand' and passed through French as a noun for goods and for the making of them.
items.cn: 这个短语意为「用手做成」，经法语成为指商品及其制作的名词。

items.en: French manufacture named the making and the thing made; English borrowed both in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语 manufacture 兼指制作与制品，英语在十七世纪两者都借入。

items.en: English added its suffix for the person or firm that performs an action, and from the eighteenth century manufacturer meant the maker of goods.
items.cn: 英语加上表示动作执行者（人或企业）的后缀，自十八世纪起这个词指商品制造者。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same verb; group two holds names for the parties that make or supply goods.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该动词的各种形式；第二组是表示制造或供应商品一方的名称。

entries.definition: The verb and the act of making, not the firm; without the agent suffix there is no doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造的动词与动作，而非企业；没有施动后缀就没有「做者」。

entries.definition: The ongoing activity or the sector, with no reference to a particular company.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续的活动或整个部门，不特指某家公司。

entries.definition: Describes goods made in a factory, or an excuse invented; it says nothing about who made them.
entries.definitionCN: 描述工厂制成的商品或编造的借口，不说明是谁造的。

entries.definition: An old word for a factory building; a manufacturer is the firm, a manufactory is the place.
entries.definitionCN: 指工厂建筑的旧词；制造商是企业，工场是地点。

entries.definition: Anyone who makes goods, films or energy; it is wider than a factory firm.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指制造商品、影片或能源的一方，比工厂企业更宽。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the one who makes something, often a craftsperson or a brand.
entries.definitionCN: 指制作某物的日常词，常指手艺人或品牌。

entries.definition: A firm that provides parts or materials to the maker rather than making the final good.
entries.definitionCN: 向制造者提供零件或材料、而非生产最终产品的企业。

entries.definition: A seller of goods, often the party that faces the buyer.
entries.definitionCN: 商品的销售方，常指面对买家的一方。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb for making goods plus the suffix for the one who does it: the firm that does the making.
normal.cn: 表示制造商品的动词加「做者」后缀：做这件事的企业。

normal.en: The family runs manufacture, manufacturing, manufactured and the adjective for what can be made.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造、制造业、制成的，以及表示可制造的形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: original equipment manufacturer, car manufacturer, drug manufacturer, warranty.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：原始设备制造商、汽车制造商、药品生产商、厂商保修。

normal.en: The word appears in three roles: the maker, the brand owner behind the shop, and the party liable for a defect.
normal.cn: 这个词出现在三种角色里：制造者、店铺背后的品牌方，以及对缺陷负责的一方。

normal.en: A firm that designs nothing may still be called the manufacturer if it builds the goods.
normal.cn: 一家不设计任何东西的企业，只要它把商品做出来，仍可能被称为制造商。

abstract.en: Picture a nameplate on a machine with only a factory name on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器的铭牌上只印着一个厂名。

abstract.en: Picture a shop handing a broken item back up the chain.
abstract.cn: 想象店铺把坏掉的物件沿链条往回递。

abstract.en: Picture one shed building parts for three different badges.
abstract.cn: 想象一座厂房为三个不同商标造零件。

examples.en: The manufacturer tested every batch before shipping.
examples.cn: 制造商在发货前检测了每一批。

examples.en: A small manufacturer can rarely afford its own retail network.
examples.cn: 小型制造商很少有能力自建零售网络。

examples.en: Under the contract, the manufacturer owns the tooling.
examples.cn: 按合同，模具归制造商所有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「manufacture（制造）+ er（做的人/厂）」——做东西的那一方 → 制造商、厂商

root: 法语来源的「制造」动词加英语施动后缀构成；该动词的拉丁底子是「手」与「做」组合成的「用手做成」短语，两个词根更早的来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one firm: it makes goods, it stands behind the brand, it builds machines, it assembles cars, it holds a drug licence, it builds for another's label, it faces the union, and it answers for defects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一家企业展开：它做商品、站在品牌背后、造机器、组装汽车、持有药品许可、替他人商标代工、面对工会，最后对缺陷负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a booth at a trade fair with a motor on a plinth and a card that carries only the factory's name.
core.cn: 核心意象：展会上的一个展台，台座上摆着一台电机，名片上只印着厂名。

chain: THE NAME SITS ON THE GOODS
THE NAME ANSWERS FOR THE GOODS

branches.en: THE MAKER: making goods and building machines are the same doer in different trades.
branches.cn: 制造者：做商品与造机器，是同一施动者处在不同行业。

branches.en: THE RESPONSIBLE NAME: the brand owner behind the shop and the licensed drug maker are both the party on record.
branches.cn: 具名的责任方：店铺背后的品牌方与持证的药品生产商，都是名义上负责的一方。

branches.en: THE ASSEMBLER: a car maker and a contract builder both put their name to goods designed elsewhere.
branches.cn: 组装者：汽车制造商与代工生产商，都把名字落到别处设计的商品上。

branches.en: THE EMPLOYER: in wage talks a group of firms speaks as one party.
branches.cn: 雇主：在工资谈判中，一群企业作为一方发言。

branches.en: THE LIABLE PARTY: product law follows the maker to the origin of the goods.
branches.cn: 责任方：产品责任法沿制造者追到商品的源头。

intro.en: Manufacturer is a Latin-rooted verb of making plus an English suffix for the doer, so it reads as hand, making, and the one who makes.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁词根的「制作」动词加英语表示「做者」的后缀，因此可读作「手」「制作」与「做这件事的一方」。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus 'hand' and facere 'make' combine in the phrase for made by hand, which French turned into a noun; English added the agent suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「手」与「做」组合成「用手做成」的短语，法语把它变成名词，英语再加上施动后缀。

items.example: The hand is the original instrument of making.
items.exampleCN: 手是最早的制作工具。

items.structure: facere, feci, factum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供动作。

items.example: French compressed the phrase into one noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语压缩成一个名词兼动词。

items.example: The suffix turns the action into a doer.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成施动者。

items.example: The doer here is a company, not a person.
items.exampleCN: 这里的施动者是公司，而不是个人。

items.example: The process noun has no doer in it.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示过程的名词不含施动者。

items.example: The participle describes the goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述商品。

items.example: The suffix marks what the process allows.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记工艺上的可行性。

definition_zh: 制造；生产；捏造；制成品；制造业
definition_en: to make goods from materials, usually in quantity, and also to invent an excuse or a story
core_image: 老厂里，工人把熔化的金属倒进模具，冷却后取出齿轮毛坯
scene: 老厂里，工人把熔化的金属倒进模具，冷却后取出齿轮毛坯。They manufacture the gears from scrap steel rather than from new billets.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「用原料加工出成品」（第 1 个义项：把材料制成物件）；句意为他们用废钢而不是新钢坯来制造这些齿轮。图中可辨识物件：熔炉、模具、齿轮毛坯、冷却水槽。

senses.title: Make goods from materials
senses.definition: to work raw materials or parts into finished objects
senses.definitionCN: 把原料或零件加工成成品
senses.example: They manufacture the gears from scrap steel rather than from new billets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用废钢而不是新钢坯来制造这些齿轮。
senses.why: The Latin phrase behind the word means made by hand, so the verb begins as making an object out of material.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「用手做成」，因此动词最初就是把材料做成物件。

senses.title: Produce in quantity
senses.definition: to make goods in large numbers by an organised process
senses.definitionCN: 通过有组织的流程大量制造商品
senses.example: The plant manufactures a million bottles a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂每月生产一百万只瓶子。
senses.why: Once making is organised in a factory, quantity becomes the point, and the verb carries that scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦制作在工厂里被组织起来，数量就成了要点，动词也就带上了这种规模。

senses.title: Assemble components into a whole
senses.definition: to put together bought-in parts into a finished unit
senses.definitionCN: 把外购零件组成一台完整设备
senses.example: The workshop manufactures frames and buys the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个车间自制车架，其余部件外购。
senses.why: Making a whole from parts is still making, even when most parts arrive finished.
senses.whyCN: 用零件做成整体仍算制作，即使大多数零件送来时已是成品。

senses.title: Produce a substance in the body
senses.definition: to generate a substance naturally, as an organ or a cell does
senses.definitionCN: 如器官或细胞那样自然生成某种物质
senses.example: The liver manufactures bile and releases it into the gut.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏合成胆汁并把它释放到肠道。
senses.why: A living organ makes a substance the way a workshop makes a product, so biology borrowed the verb.
senses.whyCN: 活体器官制造一种物质，正如作坊制造产品，因此生物学借用了这个动词。

senses.title: Invent an excuse or evidence
senses.definition: to create something false and present it as if it were true
senses.definitionCN: 编造不实之物并当作真的呈现
senses.example: He manufactured an alibi before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他在面谈之前编造了一个不在场证明。
senses.why: The sense grows from the same idea: something is made out of nothing and put forward as real.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思出自同一观念：某物从无中被做出来，并被当作真的拿出来。

senses.title: Goods, in the plural
senses.definition: products of industry, as opposed to raw materials
senses.definitionCN: 工业产品，与原材料相对
senses.example: The country exports manufactures rather than raw ore.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家出口制成品而不是原矿。
senses.why: The verb's product becomes a noun, and economists use the plural for made goods as a class.
senses.whyCN: 动词的产物变成名词，经济学家用复数形式指作为一大类的制成品。

senses.title: The industry, as a noun
senses.definition: the activity or trade of making goods, taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 制造商品的活动或行业整体
senses.example: Manufacture of cloth once paid half the town's wages.
senses.exampleCN: 布匹制造曾支付了全镇一半的工资。
senses.why: The uncountable noun names the activity itself, which is how the word stands for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词指活动本身，这个词由此代表一个行业。

senses.title: Churn out something worthless
senses.definition: to produce something quickly and in volume with little care
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的用心快速大量产出
senses.example: The studio manufactures hit songs on a yearly schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室按年度排程批量炮制热门歌曲。
senses.why: When quantity is all that matters, the same verb turns critical: making becomes mere turning out.
senses.whyCN: 当数量成为唯一要紧的事，同一个动词就带上批评意味：制作沦为「出货」。

intro.en: Manufacture came through French from the Latin phrase for made by hand, and its senses spread from handwork to factory goods to invented stories. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语「用手做成」的短语，词义从手工制品扩到工厂商品，再扩到编造的故事。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand'; its deeper root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」；其更深词根属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do'; its pre-Latin root is also reconstructed.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、制作」；其在拉丁语之前的词根也属重构形式。

items.en: The phrase meant 'made by hand', describing work of skill as opposed to what grows by itself.
items.cn: 这个短语意为「用手做成」，指凭技艺完成的工作，与自然生长之物相对。

items.en: French manufacture carried it into English in the seventeenth century for things made by hand and for the making of them.
items.cn: 法语 manufacture 在十七世纪把它带入英语，指手工制品及其制作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the verb moved to factory production; the sense of inventing something false is older and rests on the same image of making.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，动词转向工厂生产；编造不实之物的意思更早，且基于同一「做出来」的意象。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same family in other grammatical roles; group two holds verbs for making or inventing something.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词的其他词类形式；第二组是表示「制作」或「编造」的动词。

entries.definition: The agent noun for the company that carries out the making.
entries.definitionCN: 施动名词，指执行制造的企业。

entries.definition: The process or the industry, with no object and no doer named.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或行业，不点明对象与施动者。

entries.definition: A building where goods are made; it comes from the same Latin verb of making, through a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的建筑，同出拉丁「制作」动词，但走的是另一条名词路径。

entries.definition: From faber 'smith, craftsman', not from facere: it means putting parts together, or a lie.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 faber「工匠」，而非 facere：指把部件组装起来，也指谎言。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for producing anything, with no hint of factories or quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指做出任何东西的日常动词，不含工厂或数量的意味。

entries.definition: To bring forth goods, crops or results; it covers farming and energy as well.
entries.definitionCN: 产出商品、农产品或结果，也涵盖农业与能源。

entries.definition: To build a structure from parts, or to invent a story; it shares the second sense of the entry but not its first.
entries.definitionCN: 用部件搭建结构，或编造故事；与本词共用第二个义项，但不用第一个。

entries.definition: To fit components together, which is one stage inside manufacturing.
entries.definitionCN: 把零件接合起来，是制造内部的一个阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: 'Hand' plus 'make': the Latin phrase meant made by hand, and the verb kept the idea of turning material into an object.
normal.cn: 「手」加「做」：拉丁短语意为用手做成，动词保留了把材料变成物件的意思。

normal.en: The family runs manufacturer, manufacturing, manufactured and the adjective for what can be made.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造商、制造业、制成的，以及表示可制造的形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark both sides: manufacture goods, manufacture parts, manufacture an excuse.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出两面：制造商品、生产零件、编造借口。

normal.en: Making a true thing and making a false one are the same act with different material.
normal.cn: 造真东西与造假东西，是同一个动作换了材料。

normal.en: In economics the plural means made goods, and the uncountable form means the industry.
normal.cn: 在经济学里，复数指制成品，不可数形式指制造业。

abstract.en: Picture molten metal settling into the shape of a gear.
abstract.cn: 想象熔化的金属沉入齿轮的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a story assembled from spare parts, then told as fact.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用零碎部件拼成的故事，随后被当作事实讲出。

abstract.en: Picture a conveyor that never stops, and a shelf nobody inspects.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从不停下的传送带，和一个无人检查的货架。

examples.en: The firm manufactures its own sensors rather than buying them.
examples.cn: 这家公司自己制造传感器，而不是外购。

examples.en: A country that manufactures little imports almost everything.
examples.cn: 制造业薄弱的国家几乎什么都要进口。

examples.en: He manufactured a reason for leaving that nobody believed.
examples.cn: 他编了一个没人相信的离开理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「manu（手）+ fact（做）+ ure」——用手做出来的 → 制造；转而指「做出来的话」→ 捏造

root: 拉丁语中表示「手」的名词与表示「做」的动词构成「用手做成」的短语，经法语成为一词；两个词根更早的来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making: material becomes an object, quantity becomes the aim, parts become a unit, a body makes a substance, a lie is made, the products become a noun, the activity becomes an industry, and finally speed replaces care.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「做」展开：材料变成物件、数量成为目标、零件成为整机、身体合成物质、谎言被做出来、产品变成名词、活动变成行业，最后速度取代了用心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: molten metal poured into a mould and lifted out as a gear blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：熔化的金属被倒进模具，取出时已是齿轮毛坯。

branches.en: ONE OBJECT AND MANY: a single gear and a million bottles are the same making at two scales.
branches.cn: 一个与许多：一枚齿轮与一百万只瓶子，是同一种制作的两个规模。

branches.en: BUILDING A UNIT: fitting parts into a machine and an organ making a substance both assemble a whole.
branches.cn: 组成整体：把零件装成机器与器官合成物质，都在组成一个整体。

branches.en: MAKING WITHOUT MATERIAL: a false alibi and a churned-out song are made with words and speed rather than substance.
branches.cn: 不以材料制作：假的不在场证明与批量炮制的歌，用言辞与速度而非材料做成。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT AS A NOUN: made goods become a class in trade statistics.
branches.cn: 产物成为名词：制成品在贸易统计中成为一大类。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY AS AN INDUSTRY: the uncountable name stands for a whole trade.
branches.cn: 活动成为行业：不可数名称代表整个行业。

intro.en: Manufacture is a Latin phrase compressed into one French word: a noun for hand, a verb for making, and the ending that carries it into English.
intro.cn: 这是一个被压缩成一个法语词的拉丁短语：一个表示「手」的名词、一个表示「做」的动词，以及把它带进英语的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manage and manuscript; facere gives factory, fact and fabrication; together they name work made by hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「手」的词衍生出手动的、经营与手稿等词；表示「做」的动词衍生出工厂、事实与制作等词；两者合起来指用手做成的工作。

items.example: The hand is the instrument in the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 在这个短语里，手是工具。

items.structure: facere, feci, factum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb carries the action of making.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词承载「制作」的动作。

items.example: The phrase is the source of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是整词的来源。

items.example: French fused the phrase into a single noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语合成一个名词兼动词。

items.example: The ending marks the outcome of the making.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记制作的结果。

items.example: The agent suffix names the firm.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指企业。

items.example: The process suffix removes the doer.
items.exampleCN: 过程后缀去掉了施动者。

items.example: The participle carries both the factory sense and the false one.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词兼带工厂义与虚假义。

definition_zh: 工业；产业；行业；勤劳（古义）
definition_en: the making of goods in factories, and any branch of business taken as a whole
core_image: 山谷里三家工厂沿河排开，烟囱、铁路与工人宿舍连成一片
scene: 山谷里三家工厂沿着河排开，烟囱、铁路和工人宿舍连成一片。The chemical industry arrived in the valley when the railway did.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「以工厂生产为主的工业部门」（第 1 个义项：把原料加工成商品的工业整体）；句意为铁路通到山谷时，化学工业也到了这里。图中可辨识物件：厂房、烟囱、铁路线、工人宿舍。

pos.zh: 工业；产业（不可数或可数）
勤劳；勤勉（古旧义，不可数）

senses.title: Factory production as a system
senses.titleCN: 工业（以工厂生产为主的体系）
senses.definition: the organised making of goods by machines in factories
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里用机器有组织地制造商品
senses.example: The chemical industry arrived in the valley when the railway did.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路通到山谷时，化学工业也到了这里。
senses.why: The modern sense grew out of an older word for diligent activity, and it names the whole system of such activity rather than one firm.
senses.whyCN: 现代义从一个表示「勤勉活动」的旧词生长出来，指这类活动的整套体系，而非单个企业。

senses.title: A branch of business
senses.definition: a particular field of commercial activity, such as tourism or banking
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定商业领域，如旅游业或银行业
senses.example: The tourism industry hires more staff each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业每年夏天雇用更多员工。
senses.why: Once the word meant organised activity in general, any organised field of business could be called an industry.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词泛指有组织的活动，任何有组织的商业领域都可以叫一个行业。

senses.title: Firms seen against government and universities
senses.titleCN: 产业界（与政府、学界相对）
senses.definition: the business world taken as one party in policy discussions
senses.definitionCN: 在政策讨论中被当作一方的企业界
senses.example: Universities and industry share the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 大学与产业界共用这个实验室。
senses.why: A field of firms is addressed as a single party in policy talk, so a mass of businesses takes the name of the activity.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域的众多企业在政策讨论中被当作单一一方来对话，因此这群企业便用了这项活动的名称。

senses.title: The companies of one field together
senses.definition: the firms of a field considered as a group that can agree on rules
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域的公司被当作可以商定规则的整体
senses.example: The industry agreed on a common safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 该行业商定了一套共同的安全守则。
senses.why: A field's firms act together often enough that the word can mean the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一领域的公司常常一起行动，因此这个词也可以指这个群体本身。

senses.title: Diligence, in older writing
senses.definition: steady hard work, the sense the word carried before machines
senses.definitionCN: 持续刻苦地工作，是机器时代之前该词的意思
senses.example: The old essay praises industry as the root of wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文称赞勤勉是财富的根源。
senses.why: The oldest English sense was a habit of hard work, and traces of it survive in the adjective for a diligent person.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的意思是刻苦工作的习惯，这层意思仍留在表示「勤劳的」形容词里。

senses.title: A sector in economic statistics
senses.definition: one of the broad divisions of an economy, such as primary or service activity
senses.definitionCN: 经济中的一大门类，如第一产业或服务业
senses.example: Primary industry gives way to services in the statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 在统计中，第一产业让位于服务业。
senses.why: Statistical classification needs named blocks, and the word supplies the name for each block.
senses.whyCN: 统计分类需要给每一块命名，这个词就提供这些名称。

senses.title: Heavy as opposed to light production
senses.definition: the part of manufacturing that handles large machinery, fuel or metal
senses.definitionCN: 制造业中处理大型机械、燃料或金属的部分
senses.example: Heavy industry needs far more power than this grid can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 重工业需要的电力远超这张电网所能承载。
senses.why: Within factory work, a division by weight of plant and material became a fixed pair of terms.
senses.whyCN: 在工厂生产内部，按设备与材料的轻重作出的划分，成了一套固定的对举说法。

senses.title: The level of activity, as measured
senses.titleCN: 产业活动水平（统计指标）
senses.definition: the volume of production, reported as a rising or falling figure
senses.definitionCN: 生产规模，作为上升或下降的数字发布
senses.example: Industry expanded for six quarters and then stalled.
senses.exampleCN: 产业活动连续六个季度扩张，随后停滞。
senses.why: Measured output takes the name of the activity, so a chart can show industry rising without naming a firm.
senses.whyCN: 被计量的产出沿用活动的名称，因此一张图可以显示产业上升，却不点出任何企业。

intro.en: Industry came through French from Latin industria 'diligence, activity'. How that Latin word was formed is disputed, and the factory sense is only eighteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语中表示「勤勉、活动」的名词。这个拉丁词如何构成存在争议，指工厂生产的那层意思要到十八世纪才有。年代均为约数。

items.en: Industria meant 'diligence, assiduous activity, something done with effort'. It described a habit of work, not a branch of trade.
items.cn: industria 意为「勤勉、刻苦的活动、费力做成之事」，描述的是工作习惯，而非商业门类。

items.en: One long-standing suggestion reads the word as a prefix meaning 'in' plus a verb meaning 'to build'. That is a hypothesis about its shape and has not been demonstrated, so source uncertain.
items.cn: 一种流传较久的说法把这个词读作意为「在内」的前缀加意为「建造」的动词。这只是关于其构形的假说，未获证实，故来源不确定。

items.en: French industrie carried the word into English in the fifteenth century, still meaning skill and diligence in a craft.
items.cn: 法语 industrie 在十五世纪把这个词带入英语，仍指技艺上的灵巧与勤勉。

items.en: In the eighteenth century the word moved from a personal habit to the organised making of goods, and then to whole branches of it.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词从个人习惯转向有组织的商品制造，随后又转向各个制造门类。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writing fixed the modern sense: industry as the system of factories, power and mass output.
items.cn: 十九世纪的写作固定了现代义：工业即工厂、动力与大批量产出的体系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root in other roles, where two of them are easily confused; group two holds nouns for branches of economic activity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该拉丁词根的其他词类形式，其中两个极易混淆；第二组是表示经济活动门类的名词。

entries.definition: Relating to factories and mass production; it describes the system, not the effort of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与工厂和大批量生产有关，描述体系，而非个人的努力。

entries.definition: Hard-working and diligent; it kept the oldest sense while the noun moved to factories.
entries.definitionCN: 指勤奋刻苦，保留了最古老的意思，而名词已转向工厂。

entries.definition: A person who owns or controls large manufacturing businesses.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有或掌控大型制造企业的人。

entries.definition: To build factory production in a place or an economy.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地或某经济体中建立工厂生产。

entries.definition: A named part of an economy; it is the statistical term, and industry is one of its members.
entries.definitionCN: 经济中被命名的一部分，是统计术语，工业只是其中一员。

entries.definition: The activity of making goods, narrower than industry because it excludes mining and power.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的活动，比工业窄，因不含采矿与电力。

entries.definition: Commercial activity or a single firm; it need not involve factories at all.
entries.definitionCN: 商业活动或单个企业，未必涉及工厂。

entries.definition: Trade and exchange, the part of business that moves goods rather than makes them.
entries.definitionCN: 指贸易与交换，是商业中搬运商品而非制造的那部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin noun meant diligence, and diligence organised became the factory system.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词本指勤勉，被组织起来的勤勉后来成了工厂体系。

normal.en: The family splits: one adjective points at factories, another at a hard-working person.
normal.cn: 同族词分成两支：一个形容词指向工厂，另一个指向勤奋的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: heavy industry, light industry, chemical industry, tourism industry.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：重工业、轻工业、化学工业、旅游业。

normal.en: The same noun can mean one trade, all its firms, or the measured level of activity.
normal.cn: 同一名词可以指一个行业、该行业的全部企业，或被计量的活动水平。

normal.en: The older sense survives in a single adjective, which is why the pair is so often confused.
normal.cn: 较古老的意思只留在一个形容词里，这就是那一对词常被混淆的原因。

abstract.en: Picture three chimneys along a river and one railway line joining them.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的三根烟囱，由一条铁路连起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that has worked all its life, and a shed built to replace it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只劳作一生的手，和一座为取代它而建的厂房。

abstract.en: Picture a chart rising while no single factory is named.
abstract.cn: 想象一张上升的图表，却不点出任何一家工厂。

examples.en: The government wants industry to use less coal.
examples.cn: 政府希望工业少用煤。

examples.en: The film industry employs more people than the shipyards.
examples.cn: 电影业雇用的人比造船厂多。

examples.en: He owed his fortune to industry rather than to luck.
examples.cn: 他的财富来自勤勉，而非运气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「indu（在内）+ stry（建造）」——在里面不停建造 → 勤勉 → 工业、行业

root: 拉丁语中表示「勤勉、活动」的名词经法语进入英语；其为「在内」前缀加「建造」动词的读法只是假说，未获证实，故来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one organised effort: diligence becomes factory production, that production becomes a trade, the trade becomes a party in policy, a group of firms, a statistical block, a weight class, and finally a line on a chart.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份被组织起来的努力展开：勤勉变成工厂生产，生产变成一个行业，行业变成政策中的一方、一群企业、统计上的一块、按轻重分的类别，最后变成图表上的一条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three factory chimneys along a river, joined by a rail line and surrounded by workers' housing.
core.cn: 核心意象：河边三根工厂烟囱，由铁路相连，周围是工人宿舍。

branches.en: THE FACTORY SYSTEM: general factory production and the heavy end of it are the same system at two weights.
branches.cn: 工厂体系：泛指工厂生产与其中的重工业，是同一体系的两个轻重档。

branches.en: ONE TRADE AND ITS FIRMS: a branch of business and the companies inside it are the same group seen as activity and as members.
branches.cn: 一个行业与其企业：商业门类与其中的公司，是同一群体被看作活动与成员。

branches.en: A PARTY IN POLICY: the business world speaks as one voice against government and universities.
branches.cn: 政策中的一方：企业界对政府与学界作为同一个声音说话。

branches.en: THE OLD HABIT: diligence is the personal virtue the word started from.
branches.cn: 古老的习惯：勤勉是这个词出发时的个人德性。

branches.en: THE STATISTICAL BLOCK: a sector in a table and a rising line on a chart are the same output counted twice.
branches.cn: 统计上的一块：表格中的部门与图表上上升的线，是同一产出被计了两次。

intro.en: Industry is a Latin noun of diligent activity taken into French and English; its family splits between the factory adjective and the diligent-person adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示勤勉活动的拉丁名词，经法语进入英语；其词族分成「工厂的」与「勤劳的」两支形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria yields industrial, industrialize and industrialization, while the same stem also gives the adjective for a hard-working person.
latinIntro.cn: 这个拉丁名词衍生出工业的、使工业化与工业化等词；同一词干还给出表示勤奋的形容词。

items.example: The noun begins as a virtue, not a trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词起初是一种德性，而非行业。

items.example: The adjective describes the person the noun praised.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述名词所称赞的人。

items.example: French added the sense of a craft and then a trade.
items.exampleCN: 法语加进了「技艺」，再扩展到「行业」。

items.meaning: organised making; a branch of trade
items.meaningCN: 有组织的制造；商业门类
items.example: English kept both the old virtue and the new system.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留旧的德性与新的体系。

items.example: The suffix makes the factory adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示工厂的形容词。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective for a diligent person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示勤劳的形容词。

items.example: The verb marks the change to factory production.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词标记转向工厂生产的变化。

items.example: The person suffix names the owner of large works.
items.exampleCN: 表示人的后缀指大型工厂的所有者。

items.example: The noun names the whole changeover.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指整场转变。

definition_en: the whole sequence of suppliers, transport, storage and sellers that brings a product from raw material to the user
core_image: 货轮卸下零件，卡车送进仓库，最后由快递把包裹放到买家门口
scene: 货轮把零件运到港口，卡车再送进仓库，最后由快递送到买家门口。The supply chain broke at the port, and every factory downstream idled for a week.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「从原料到用户之间的整条供应与流转链条」（第 1 个义项：把供应、运输、仓储与销售串起来的整体序列）；句意为港口那一环断了，下游每家工厂都停了一周。图中可辨识物件：货轮、港口吊机、卡车、仓库、快递包裹。

senses.title: The whole path from material to user
senses.titleCN: 从原料到用户的整条路径
senses.definition: every step, firm and movement that a product passes through before it reaches the buyer
senses.definitionCN: 产品到达买家之前所经过的每一步、每一家企业和每一次运输
senses.example: The supply chain broke at the port, and every factory downstream idled for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 港口那一环断了，下游每家工厂都停了一周。
senses.why: Supply is what is provided and a chain is links joined in order, so the phrase names the whole ordered path of provision.
senses.whyCN: 前一个词指被提供之物，后一个词指按顺序相接的环节，因此这个短语指供应的整条有序路径。

senses.title: One product's network of firms
senses.definition: the particular set of suppliers and carriers that serves one product line
senses.definitionCN: 为某一条产品线服务的那一组供应商与承运方
senses.example: Each model has its own supply chain of two hundred suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 每个型号都有自己的供应链，涉及两百个供应商。
senses.why: Different products use different links, so the same phrase can name a specific network rather than the general idea.
senses.whyCN: 不同产品使用不同环节，因此同一短语也可以指一个具体网络，而非泛泛的概念。

senses.title: The management function
senses.definition: the business function that plans and controls these flows
senses.definitionCN: 规划与控制这些流动的商业职能
senses.example: The firm treats supply chain as a function, not a cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把供应链当作一项职能，而不是一项成本。
senses.why: A function is named after the flow it plans, so the people who arrange provision are said to run the supply chain.
senses.whyCN: 职能以它所规划的流动命名，因此安排供给的人被说成在管供应链。

senses.title: The upstream end
senses.definition: the part of the path nearest the raw materials, where risk often hides
senses.definitionCN: 路径中最靠近原料的那一段，风险常藏在这里
senses.example: The weakest link sits at the far end of the supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 最弱的一环位于供应链的最远端。
senses.why: A chain has ends, and the end nearest extraction is called upstream because goods flow down from it.
senses.whyCN: 链条有两端，最靠近采掘的那一端因为货物流向下方而被称为上游。

senses.title: The risk of interruption
senses.definition: the exposure of this path to a failure at any one link
senses.definitionCN: 这条路径因任一环节失效而承受的风险
senses.example: Banks now ask how the supply chain would survive a flood.
senses.exampleCN: 银行现在会问，这条供应链在洪水中能否撑住。
senses.why: Once a path can be broken, the path itself becomes the thing exposed, so the phrase names the risk rather than the route.
senses.whyCN: 一条路径一旦可能断裂，路径本身就成了暴露在风险中的东西，因此该短语指风险而非路线。

senses.title: A short, local path
senses.definition: a deliberately shortened path, often regional, that reduces dependence on distant links
senses.definitionCN: 有意缩短、常为区域性的路径，以减少对远方环节的依赖
senses.example: The region rebuilt a short supply chain for vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区为蔬菜重建了一条短供应链。
senses.why: If distance is the problem, shortening the path is the remedy, and the phrase takes the adjective short.
senses.whyCN: 若距离是问题，缩短路径就是办法，这个短语便带上「短」的修饰。

senses.title: The tracked, visible path
senses.definition: the same path made visible from origin to shelf by tags and data
senses.definitionCN: 借助标签与数据，把从产地到货架的同一路径变得可见
senses.example: Tracking tags make the supply chain visible from ore to shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 追踪标签让供应链从矿石到货架都可见。
senses.why: A path you cannot see cannot be managed, so visibility became a property of the chain itself.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的路径无法管理，因此「可见」成了链条本身的一种属性。

senses.title: A path shared between rivals
senses.definition: a path in which competing firms use the same suppliers or carriers
senses.definitionCN: 竞争企业共用同一批供应商或承运方的路径
senses.example: Two rivals share one supply chain for batteries.
senses.exampleCN: 两家竞争对手共用一条电池供应链。
senses.why: When the same links serve different brands, the chain belongs to no single firm, which is the collaborative sense.
senses.whyCN: 当同一批环节服务不同品牌时，链条不属于任何一家企业，这就是协作义。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of filling up from below with a Latin noun for a linked series. Both halves are old words; the pair is a twentieth-century business term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语中表示「从下面补足」的动词与表示「相连序列」的名词连在一起。两半都是古老的词，合起来则是二十世纪的商业术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plere meant 'to fill'. Its pre-Latin root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: plere 意为「填满」。其在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，故来源不确定。

items.en: Sub- 'from below' plus plere 'fill' gave supplere, 'to fill up, to make complete, to furnish what is lacking'.
items.cn: sub-「从下面」加 plere「填满」构成 supplere，意为「补足、使完整、提供所缺之物」。

items.en: Catena meant 'a chain'. Its own origin is not settled; the link to any Indo-European root is a reconstruction, so source uncertain.
items.cn: catena 意为「链条」。其自身来源没有定论；与任何印欧词根的联系都属重构，故来源不确定。

items.en: Old French chaine carried the noun into English, where a chain is a series of linked parts or shops.
items.cn: 古法语 chaine 把这个名词带入英语，chain 指一串相连的环节或店铺。

items.en: Business writing of the later twentieth century joined the two nouns to describe the whole path of provision, and the term then spread to risk, finance and traceability.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的商业写作把这两个名词连用，描述供应的整条路径，此后该术语扩及风险、金融与可追踪性。

note.en: Group one holds compounds that also describe a linked path of business activity; group two holds words for the parts of that path.
note.cn: 第一组是同样描述商业活动链条的复合词；第二组是表示这条路径各环节的词。

entries.definition: The sequence of steps in which worth is added to a product; it follows money rather than goods.
entries.definitionCN: 指产品被逐步增值的序列，跟随的是钱而不是货。

entries.definition: The same path described from the customer's order backwards to the supplier.
entries.definitionCN: 同一条路径，从客户订单往回描述到供应商。

entries.definition: A web of suppliers rather than a single line, used when firms buy from many directions.
entries.definitionCN: 指网状的多向供应关系，用于企业从多个方向采购的情形。

entries.definition: Relating to production and incentives to produce; it is a policy term, not a physical path.
entries.definitionCN: 指生产及生产激励，是政策术语，不是实物路径。

entries.definition: The transport, storage and scheduling that carries goods along the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿链条搬运货物的运输、仓储与调度。

entries.definition: The act of obtaining goods and services, one function inside the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指获取商品与服务的行为，是链条内的一项职能。

entries.definition: The part that moves finished goods to shops and buyers.
entries.definitionCN: 指把成品送到店铺与买家的那一段。

entries.definition: The search for and choice of suppliers, which fixes the shape of the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻找并选定供应商，决定了链条的形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first noun means filling up what is lacking; the second means a series of links.
normal.cn: 前一个名词指补足所缺，后一个名词指一串相接的环节。

normal.en: The family runs supply, supplier, sourcing and the verb for providing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括供应、供应商、寻源，以及表示提供的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: management, disruption, risk, visibility, upstream.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：供应链管理、供应链中断、供应链风险、供应链可视化、上游。

normal.en: A chain is only as strong as its weakest link, which is why the word is used for risk.
normal.cn: 链条的强度取决于最弱的一环，因此这个词常与风险连用。

normal.en: The phrase can mean the general idea, one product's network, or a single firm's function.
normal.cn: 这个短语可以指一般概念、某一产品的网络，或某家公司的职能。

abstract.en: Picture a single parcel that has passed through six pairs of hands before reaching a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹在到达一扇门之前经过了六双手。

abstract.en: Picture one broken link and a whole line of machines standing still.
abstract.cn: 想象一个环节断掉，整排机器静止不动。

abstract.en: Picture two competing badges fed by the same conveyor.
abstract.cn: 想象两个互相竞争的商标由同一条传送带供料。

examples.en: The report maps the supply chain from mine to shop.
examples.cn: 报告把从矿场到商店的供应链画了出来。

examples.en: A longer supply chain means more places where it can fail.
examples.cn: 供应链越长，可能出问题的地方就越多。

examples.en: They shortened the supply chain by buying from nearby farms.
examples.cn: 他们向附近农场采购，缩短了供应链。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「supply（供应）+ chain（链条）」——一环扣一环的供应路径 → 供应链

root: 英语复合短语：前半底子是拉丁语「从下面补足」的动词，由意为「从下面」的前缀与「填满」动词构成；后半底子是拉丁语「链条」名词，其自身来源无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one path: the whole route from material to buyer, one product's own network, the office that manages it, its upstream end, its exposure to failure, a deliberately short version, a tracked version, and a version shared by rivals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条路径展开：从原料到买家的整条路线、某一产品自己的网络、管理它的部门、它的上游一端、它面对的中断风险、有意缩短的版本、可追踪的版本，以及被竞争对手共用的版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container unloaded at a quay, carried by lorry to a warehouse, then handed to a courier at a front door.
core.cn: 核心意象：集装箱在码头卸下，由卡车送到仓库，最后在前门交给快递员。

branches.en: THE WHOLE ROUTE: the phrase's basic sense is the complete path from extraction to the buyer.
branches.cn: 整条路线：这个短语的基本义就是从采掘到买家的完整路径。

branches.en: A NETWORK WITH ENDS: one product's set of suppliers has an upstream end where risk concentrates.
branches.cn: 有端点的网络：某一产品的供应商集合有一个风险集中的上游端点。

branches.en: WHO OWNS THE PATH: a managed function belongs to one firm, while a shared chain belongs to none.
branches.cn: 谁拥有路径：被管理的职能属于一家企业，而被共用的链条不属于任何一家。

branches.en: SEEING THE RISK: exposure to failure and tracking from ore to shelf are the same concern, one before and one after the break.
branches.cn: 看见风险：中断风险与从矿石到货架的可追踪，是同一份担忧，一个在断裂前，一个在断裂后。

branches.en: SHORTENING: a local path is the same chain with fewer links.
branches.cn: 缩短：本地路径就是环节更少的同一条链条。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin-rooted nouns: one for filling a lack, one for a series of links, which together describe provision as a path.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁词根的名词构成：一个表示「补足所缺」，一个表示「一串环节」，合起来把供应描述成一条路径。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplere gives supply, supplier and supplement; Latin catena gives chain and the idea of linked series.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「补足」的动词衍生出供应、供应商与补充物；拉丁语表示「链条」的名词衍生出链条以及「相连序列」的观念。

items.example: The prefix places the filling beneath the lack.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「填补」放在缺口的下方。

items.structure: plere, plevi, pletum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the idea of completing a shortage.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「补足短缺」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole first noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是前半名词的来源。

items.example: The noun and verb both name provision.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词都指供给。

items.example: The noun supplies the image of links in order.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「环节按序相接」的意象。

items.example: The word covers metal links and linked shops alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼指金属链环与连锁店铺。

items.example: The agent suffix names the firm at the start of a link.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指链条起点处的企业。

items.example: The compound is a twentieth-century business term.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是二十世纪的商业术语。

definition_en: the detailed organisation of moving, storing and supplying things, especially for an army or a large business
core_image: 仓库里叉车按路线取货，货车在月台排队，调度员盯着屏幕上每一票货物的位置
scene: 仓库里叉车按路线取货，货车在月台排队，调度员盯着屏幕上每一票货物的位置。Good logistics kept the relief supplies moving through three flooded counties.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「把货物运输、仓储与调度组织起来的实务」（第 1 个义项：使货物按时到达的整体安排）；句意为良好的物流让救援物资穿过三个受淹的县。图中可辨识物件：叉车、月台、排队的货车、调度屏。

pos.zh: 物流；后勤（不可数，形式为复数）

senses.title: The organisation of moving goods
senses.titleCN: 货物运输与仓储的组织
